The Nvidia scandal has sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley as well as the political establishment
Alice Huang, a suspected China spy who has been linked to Nvidia's former boss Jensen Huang, left her executive role at Megaspeed in August last year, the company says.
Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees.
Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.
Megaspeed said it was aware of reports "containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence".
It added that it "conducts legitimate and lawful business" and has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation".
Alice Huang stepped down from her role as director of Megaspeed near the end of 2023, according to Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS but it said she was still "practically in control" of the company.
Alice Huang - who is of no relation to Nvidia's former boss - had been investigated by Singapore authorities in February 2025 as part of the country's probe into Megaspeed and other companies.
Also on Sunday, US Congressman John Moolenaar said that Jensen Huang had agreed to testify before the House Select Committee on China, which he chairs, as well as the Foreign Affairs and the Intelligence committees.
The committees had threatened to issue subpoenas to Jensen Huang if he did not comply with their requests to testify.
Moolenaar told CBS, BBC's US partner, that none were ultimately issued.
Jensen Huang's testimony is expected to take place behind close doors, with the dates still being finalised.
Moolenaar said: "That's going to be a very important meeting to understand to what degree privileged information was accessed, and to what degree this potential alleged Chinese spy influenced Nvidia's philosophy and may have had an influence on some of our policies with respect to AI and export controls."
Separately, a group of tech leaders including Space X's Elon Musk, have been trying to rally support to have Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia's chief executive.
A representative forJensen Huang declined to comment on a report in the Financial Times suggesting that he was discussing a comeback to the firm he co-founded.
The BBC understands that the likelihood of him being reinstated is very low while the company's internal investigations are ongoing.
The move would also face scrutiny from Washington, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent calling for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.
For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday, 17 November.
On Friday, Bessent blamed the US Commerce Department, led by fellow cabinet colleague Howard Lutnick, for failing to properly oversee the export of high-end chips.
Bessent told CNBC that several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months... but Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process".
The so-called entity list restricts US trade with overseas firms and individuals.
Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over his department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.
Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Jensen Huang.
Megaspeed is suspected of giving backdoor access to Nvidia chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?
Nvidia has been banned from selling its advanced semiconductors to China.
While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.
Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations.
Megaspeed said it "designs and maintains its global operational and supply-chain control frameworks to comply with all applicable laws and regulatory regimes". It said this includes "US export control requirements and local jurisdiction rules in every market where we operate".
China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.

The AI-powered Ask Maps feature can suggest stops for your next trip, while providing real-time details about each location.
Google is launching a new AI trip-planning feature for Maps that allows the app to create custom itineraries for you and provide real-time details about each stop. The update, which is rolling out to the Gemini-powered Ask Maps chatbot inside the app, lets you plan a one-day outing or a trip spanning several days.
As an example, Google says you can use Ask Maps to plan a day trip for holiday shopping, or have it create a schedule for a three-day road trip with stops for coastal hikes and oceanfront dining. From there, Ask Maps will generate a day-by-day schedule with a list of stops, while also showing your route and numbered pins for each location on the map. You can share the itinerary with friends or family members, as well as export it to Google Docs on desktop.
You can ask Maps to show your trip schedule before you leave, or select the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. Along with directions, Google Maps will display real-time information about traffic, a location’s hours, and more. You can also view “know before you go” details about parking, car charging, weather conditions, potential delays, and tolls during your trip.
In addition to trip planning, you can now use Ask Maps to find specific beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments, and have it call the locations for you. You can also use Ask Maps to find saved places on your list by asking something like, “Which spots on saved in my lists have availability for five people in the next 30 minutes?”
Google is expanding Ask Maps to over 30 countries in Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. Trip-planning and saved list search is rolling out to the more than 200 countries where Ask Maps is available, while “know before you go” tips and appointment-finding are launching in the US to start.

Şirketten yapılan açıklamaya göre, Türk Telekom, COP31'de üstlendiği küresel dijital dönüşüm ve teknoloji destekçiliği kapsamında zirvenin dijital altyapısını uçtan uca yönetiyor.
Bu kapsamda, Türk Telekom, güçlü fiber ve mobil altyapısı, yeni nesil teknolojileri ve mühendislik birikimiyle uluslararası katılımcıları Antalya'dan dünyaya bağlıyor.
Türk Telekom, 1,1 milyon metrekarelik zirve alanında 1,3 milyon metre fiber hat, 400 Gbps bağlantı kapasitesi, 1800 kablosuz erişim noktası ve 18 mobil baz istasyonuyla organizasyonun dijital ihtiyaçlarını karşılıyor.
Türk Telekom'un teknoloji gücü ve operasyonel kabiliyetini zirvenin ilk haftasında gerçekleşen dijital iletişim verileri de ortaya koydu.
COP31'in ilk haftasında toplam 380 terabaytlık (TB) veri trafiği gerçekleşirken, mobil şebeke üzerinden 130 TB'lık kullanım, sabit ağ üzerinden ise 250 TB veri trafiği kaydedildi.
Zirvede, Birleşmiş Milletler'in liderler zirvesi etkinliklerine ev sahipliği yapan Mavi Bölge'de eş zamanlı bağlı cihaz sayısı da 27 bin 794'e ulaşarak, COP organizasyonları tarihindeki en yüksek seviyeye çıktı.
Açıklamada görüşlerine yer verilen Türk Telekom CEO'su Ebubekir Şahin, Türk Telekom'un 185 yılı aşkın geçmişinden aldıkları güç ve birikimle Türkiye'nin dijital geleceğini inşa etme sorumluluğunu kararlılıkla sürdürdüklerini belirtti.
Şahin, Türkiye'nin teknoloji alanındaki potansiyelini küresel platformlara taşımayı, yerli mühendislik gücüyle teknolojik yetkinlikleri uluslararası ölçekte görünür kılmayı önemsediklerini vurguladı.
"Yarına Sözümüz Var" yaklaşımıyla dijital dönüşümün sunduğu fırsatları toplumun tüm kesimleri için değere dönüştürdüklerini anlatan Şahin, teknolojinin daha sürdürülebilir bir geleceğe katkı sağlamasına öncülük ettiklerini aktardı.
Şahin, bu vizyon doğrultusunda COP31 gibi tüm dünyanın takip ettiği bir organizasyonun Küresel Dijital Dönüşüm ve Teknoloji destekçisi olmaktan gurur duyduklarının altını çizerek, şunları kaydetti:
"Geleceğimizin şekilleneceği bu küresel organizasyonda yalnızca iletişim altyapısını sağlayan bir operatör olarak değil, mühendislik gücümüz, enerji verimliliğine odaklanan yenilikçi çözümlerimiz, operasyonel yetkinliğimiz ve sürdürülebilirlik vizyonumuzla sürecin önemli paydaşlarından biri olarak yer alıyoruz. Fiber ve mobil ağımızdan yeni nesil bağlantı teknolojilerine, veri merkezi kapasitemizden, network ve siber güvenlik operasyonlarına uzanan bütüncül bir sistemle zirvenin dijital ihtiyaçları için yüksek kapasite, hız ve güvenlik sunuyoruz. Dünya Antalya'da iklim değişikliğini ve geleceği konuşurken, zirvedeki bu konuşmaları teknoloji gücümüzle Antalya'dan tüm dünyaya taşıyoruz. Bu büyük operasyonu kesintisiz ve güvenilir biçimde sürdürmek için 2 bin arkadaşımız sahada görev yapıyor."
Organizasyonun ilk haftasında ortaya çıkan kullanım verilerinin de şirketin teknoloji yatırımlarının, güçlü altyapının ve operasyonel yetkinliğinin somut bir göstergesi niteliğinde olduğuna işaret eden Şahin, Türkiye'nin teknoloji alanındaki birikimini ve dijital yetkinliğini her alanda güçlü biçimde temsil etmeyi sürdüreceklerini ifade etti.
Anadolu Ajansı web sitesinde, AA Haber Akış Sistemi (HAS) üzerinden abonelere sunulan haberler, özetlenerek yayımlanmaktadır. Abonelik için lütfen iletişime geçiniz.
Bu haberde bir hata mı var? Her türlü talep, şikâyet ve görüş için okur temsilcimize ulaşabilirsiniz.

Apple , insanların yapay zekayı sağlık alanında nasıl kullandıklarını incelemek üzere yeni bir uygulama başlattı
OpenAI ve Anthropic gibi büyük yapay zeka laboratuvarları, sağlıkla ilgili soruları yanıtlayabilen ve özel işlevler sunan sohbet robotlarına odaklanmış durumda. Apple ise insanların yapay zekayı sağlık amacıyla nasıl kullandıklarını anlamak için yeni bir çalışma başlatıyor. Ancak şirket, diğer yapay zeka girişimlerinden farklı bir yol izliyor; klinik temelli yanıtların insanlara nasıl yardımcı olabileceğini araştırmayı hedefliyor.
iPhone üreticisi, sağlık odaklı yapay zeka şirketi OpenEvidence ile iş birliği yaparak yeni bir araştırma uygulaması sunuyor. Apple; ABD'de yaşayan, 21 yaş ve üzeri, iPhone 15 veya daha yeni bir model kullanan, iOS 26 veya daha güncel bir işletim sistemi sürümüne sahip olan ve Apple Intelligence özelliği etkinleştirilmiş kullanıcıları bu çalışmaya davet ediyor. Şirket, 12 aydan uzun sürmesi planlanan bu çalışmaya 200 bine kadar katılımcı dahil etmeyi hedefliyor.
Yeni uygulama, kullanıcıların tıpkı ChatGPT veya Claude'da olduğu gibi sağlıkla ilgili sorular sormalarına olanak tanıyor. Uygulamanın sunduğu yanıtlar; The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association ve Nature gibi kaynaklardan alınan klinik verilere dayanıyor. Apple, uygulamanın günlük tıbbi sorulara basitleştirilmiş yanıtlar vermeyi amaçladığını belirtti. Kullanıcılar, bu yanıtları puanlayıp geri bildirimde bulunabilecek; ayrıca aylık anketlere katılmaları da istenecek. Yapay zekâ tarafından hazırlanan yanıtların yanında ilgili bilimsel araştırmalara ve tıbbi kaynaklara bağlantılar da gösteriliyor.
Katılımcılar; dinlenme halindeki kalp atış hızı, fiziksel aktivite, uyku düzeni veya laboratuvar sonuçları gibi HealthKit verilerini paylaşarak uygulamadan daha kişiselleştirilmiş ve hedefe yönelik öneriler alabilirler. Şirket, uygulamanın katılımcıların doktor ziyaretlerine daha iyi hazırlanmalarına yardımcı olabileceğini ve endişe verici tıbbi sorunlarla ilgili konularda kullanıcıları ilgili sağlık uzmanlarına yönlendireceğini ifade etti.
Apple, verilerin güvenli bir üçüncü taraf bulut sağlayıcısına gönderilmeden önce anonimleştirileceğini ve hiçbir yapay zeka modelini eğitmek için kullanılmayacağını vurguladı. Şirket, OpenEvidence'ın sorgu ve yanıt verilerini 24 saat sonra sildiğini belirtti.
Apple’ın Sağlık ve Fitness’tan Sorumlu Başkan Yardımcısı Dr. Sumbul Desai yaptığı açıklamada, “Apple olarak, sorumlu inovasyonun bilimsel titizlik ve klinik temellere dayanması gerektiğine inanıyoruz. Sağlık son derece kişisel bir konudur; insanların günlük yaşamlarında sağlık odaklı yapay zekâ ile nasıl etkileşim kurduklarını, onu nasıl algılayıp değerlendirdiklerini anlamanın en özenli yolu ise özel bir araştırma çalışması yürütmektir. Bu çalışmadan elde edilecek bulgular, daha geniş kapsamlı bilimsel tartışmalara katkı sağlayacak; ayrıca teknoloji geliştikçe, insanların sağlık yolculuklarının hangi aşamasında olurlarsa olsunlar, onları gerçekten destekleyen güvenilir araçlar geliştirmeye devam etmemizi güvence altına alacaktır” açıklamasını yaptı.

İtalya, Android kullanıcılarının galerilerindeki fotoğraf ve videoları Facebook'ta, belirli bir onay veya yeterli bilgilendirme olmadan kullandığı için Meta'ya €805 million para cezası verdi.
İtalya Veri Koruma Otoritesi, "Facebook'ta gezinirken galeriden öneriler al" adı verilen özelliğin, ePrivacy direktifi olarak bilinen Avrupa gizlilik direktifini ihlal ettiğini açıkladı.
Otorite, akıllı telefonların bir kişinin özel alanının parçası olarak korunduğunu ve bu tür bir erişim için "özgür ve bilgilendirilmiş rıza" gerektiğini belirtti.
Soruşturmayı yürüten yetkililer, özelliğin varsayılan olarak etkin olduğunu ve Facebook'un galeri erişimini, farklı amaçlara hizmet eden birden fazla uygulama işlevini kapsayan tek bir izinle talep ettiğini tespit etti.
Otorite, Meta'ya özelliği devre dışı bırakması ve kullanımı için ayrı bir onay alması amacıyla 60 gün süre verdi. Kuruma göre İtalya'da yaklaşık 20 milyon Android kullanıcısı bulunuyor.
Açıklamaya göre para cezası, İtalya'nın yetkisini sorgulayan Meta Platforms Ireland Limited'e uygulandı.
Otorite, Meta'nın soruşturmaya yönelik "işbirliği eksikliğinin" de cezaya etki ettiğini ve cezanın, grubun küresel cirosunun yaklaşık yüzde 0,47'sine karşılık geldiğini bildirdi.
Süreçte, kullanıcı içeriklerinin yapay zeka modellerini eğitmek için olası kullanımına ilişkin herhangi bir inceleme yapılmadı; Meta ayrıca böyle bir şey yaptığını reddediyor.
Meta, karara itiraz edeceğini söyledi. Meta sözcüsü, şirketin düzenleyici kurumun değerlendirmesine, yasanın yorumlanmasına ve "cezanın orantısız düzeyine" "şiddetle katılmadığını" ifade etti.
Meta, yaptığı açıklamada, "Bu, insanların Facebook'ta fotoğraf ve video paylaşmasına yardımcı olan basit bir özelliktir" dedi.
Meta, "Kullanıcıların, özellik çalışmadan önce cihazlarında izin vermesi gerekiyor ve bu izni istedikleri zaman ayarlarından değiştirebiliyorlar" diye ekledi.
Soruşturma, Bolzano Consumer Protection Centre'den gelen şikayet üzerine Temmuz 2025'te başlatıldı ve İtalyan yetkililer tarafından yapılan teknik analize dayandırıldı.

Riders in Las Vegas can hail Amazon-owned Zoox’s steering-wheel-free robotaxis through the Uber app — with an MGM Resorts partnership and a 2027 Los Angeles expansion on the way.
Uber may be breaking up with Waymo, but it’s also gaining a new robotaxi BFF : Amazon. Starting today, Uber riders in Las Vegas can be matched with Amazon-owned Zoox’s purpose-built, bidirectional robotaxis.
It’s a first for both companies: the first time Uber is adding a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle to its network, and the first time that Zoox is opening up its fleet to a third-party app . Uber says that anyone ordering an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save in Sin City can get matched with a Zoox at no extra charge. Just like with Uber’s other AV partnerships (like Waymo in Phoenix and Austin, for now), riders can toggle a preference in the app’s Ride Preferences settings to boost their chances of getting an autonomous pod.
Unlike Uber’s human drivers, Zoox has some geographic limitations. The company’s robotaxis only cover heavy tourist zones, like the Strip, downtown Las Vegas, and the Arts District. And Zoox isn’t abandoning its standalone app; it will continue to operate independently alongside the Uber integration.
Alongside the launch, Uber and Zoox announced a multiyear deal making them the official rideshare and robotaxi partners for MGM Resorts International in Las Vegas. Anyone who has ever tried to catch a ride at the Bellagio or MGM Grand knows that resort pickup zones are notoriously chaotic. For autonomous vehicles, navigating sprawling, poorly mapped casino entrances — where valets, idling tour buses, and confused tourists all mill about — is a major technical headache.
To keep Zoox’s pods from getting stuck in endless resort traffic loops, the partnership goes beyond simple branding. MGM, Uber, and Zoox say they are rolling out physical infrastructure tweaks, like clearer on-property wayfinding and custom in-app guidance designed to make pickups and drop-offs actually work smoothly for driverless cars.
Uber and Zoox aren’t stopping at Vegas. The two companies already have their eyes their next major market: Los Angeles. Zoox plans to launch initial standalone operations in LA through its own app before the end of 2026, followed by a full Uber integration sometime in 2027.
Uber’s playbook of welcoming a variety of small and large robotaxi players into its app came after the company pivoted away from building its own self-driving tech. Now it’s attempting to position itself as an indispensable platform for every autonomous vehicle operator, including Motional , WeRide , Avride , and Zoox.
Of course, Uber’s strategy has had some drawbacks, too. Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana recently announced an end to her company’s exclusive partnership with Uber in Austin and Atlanta by January 2028, calling it a “crapshoot.”

Google announced on Monday that it’s rolling out new Maps features that are designed to help people plan trips and everyday tasks using AI. The company is launching the ability for Maps to create trip itineraries and find appointments for users.
The new features reflect a broader shift in how tech companies are positioning AI, which is less as a tool that just answers questions and more as an assistant that can complete tasks on users’ behalf. While many companies have released AI agents to complete these tasks, Google is working to bring that approach into a service that millions of people already use every day.
Google says users can use the navigation platform’s “Ask Maps” tool to build step-by-step trip itineraries and get real-time details about their route right when they pull up directions.
For example, you could use Ask Maps to plan a holiday shopping day trip or something more complex, like a three-day road trip featuring coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Google says. You’ll get a day-by-day itinerary with insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop. Once you’re happy with your itinerary, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.
When you’re ready to head out, you can use Ask Maps to reopen your itinerary or find the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. You’ll have access to real-time information, including traffic conditions, business hours, and a look at what the “vibe” is at your next stop, the company says. You could also adjust your schedule by asking Maps to do something like add a scenic viewpoint or lunch stop along your route. You can then tap any destination in your itinerary to get directions and navigate to your next stop.
Additionally, users can use Ask Maps to find beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments online and call local businesses for you. For example, you could ask: “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me.” Ask Maps will then display open slots across nearby businesses.
The new agentic calling feature arrives as tech companies continue to introduce AI agents designed to handle time-consuming tasks, such as scheduling DMV appointments and making reservations. For example, Meta’s AI agent Muse recently gained the ability to call businesses on users’ behalf.
Google also announced that you can now use Ask Maps to quickly find places on your lists by asking something like: “Which spots saved in my lists have availability for five people in the next 30 minutes?”
The tech giant says the new updates are starting to roll out on Monday on Android and iOS. As part of the news, Google announced that Ask Maps is expanding to 30 countries across Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the U.K.

Zoox robotaxis are officially available through the Uber app in Las Vegas, marking the Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle company’s first partnership with a third-party ride-hailing platform.
The launch on Monday is a milestone for both companies. Uber gets to add another partner to its app as part of its broader strategy to become the primary purveyor of autonomous vehicle technology in North America, Europe, and the Middle East. Uber has partnered with more than 30 companies developing autonomous vehicle technology for sidewalk delivery robots, self-driving cars, robotaxis, and drones — though not all of those have turned into commercial deployments yet.
For Zoox, the partnership and launch gives it access to more potential customers who might otherwise not try its robotaxi, a needed boost as it trails market leaders Tesla and Waymo.
The partnership is expected to extend beyond Las Vegas. Zoox will begin initial robotaxi operations in Los Angeles this year (introducing the robotaxi and opening rides to Zoox employees, family, and friends), but commercial service will not begin until 2027. Rides will be available via the Uber app next year as well.
For now, all eyes are on Las Vegas, Zoox’s first commercial market and a city where Uber has ambitious robotaxi plans.
The two companies also announced a multi-year partnership with MGM Resorts International: they’re rideshare and robotaxi partners for MGM Resorts properties in Las Vegas. Uber and Zoox said they’ll work with MGM Resorts to improve pickup and drop-off locations, along with signage to help riders navigate sprawling MGM properties and find the robotaxis.
Earlier this year, the Nevada Transportation Authority unanimously approved a permit that allowed Uber to deploy up to 1,000 robotaxis in Clark County — home to Las Vegas — through its partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox.
Zoox’s addition to the Uber app comes with some initial limitations. Customers won’t be able to select a Zoox robotaxi — at least initially. Instead, people who request an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric, or Wait & Save ride may be matched with one of Zoox’s custom-built robotaxis once they hail a ride. Customers can increase their chances of getting a Zoox robotaxi by opting for autonomous rides through “ride preferences” in the Uber app’s settings.
Uber plans to introduce a dedicated autonomous option in its app as “availability and reliability improve,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call in November.
“Las Vegas will become the first U.S. city where riders can access two fully driverless partners through the Uber app,” he said on the call. “We will begin with limited fleets and expand supply over the coming months, with plans to introduce a dedicated autonomous option in our app.”
The plan to offer a dedicated autonomous option marks a shift in Uber’s approach to robotaxis, including its partnership with Waymo.
That exclusive partnership, which matches Waymo robotaxis with Uber riders in Austin and Atlanta, will end in January 2028. Waymo plans to offer its rides directly through its own smartphone app as it does in other cities. TechCrunch previously confirmed with Uber that it still plans to host Waymo robotaxis on its app for as long as the two companies agree.
And unlike its partnership with other AV developers, Uber told TechCrunch that it will not provide maintenance and other services for Zoox in the Las Vegas market.

The study will be conducted through a new app where participants can ask health questions and rate the responses.
Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence , a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine . Participants will use a new iOS app to ask medical questions and then rate the responses based on criteria including accuracy, detail, and relevance.
The app is now available for download, and enrollment starts today, with Apple looking for up to 200,000 people to contribute. Participants 21 and older must be based in the US, and although the app doesn’t use Apple Intelligence, it does require an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 26 or later.
Study participants can use the app to ask health-related questions and receive easily understandable responses with links to peer-reviewed clinical sources. The app relies on text-based prompts, and while dictation is an option using the iOS keyboard, the app isn’t integrated with Siri or Apple Intelligence.
During enrolment, participants are given the option to share Apple HealthKit data, like their activity, sleep, or clinical lab results, so responses will include more context about their own personal health. But privacy is a priority, and Apple says it has taken measures to ensure users’ information remains confidential and the data collected won’t be used to train AI models. The aim is to improve the design and functionality of AI-powered health tools so they can deliver relevant health information that’s easier for users to understand and act on.
“At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life. Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” said Sumbul Desai, MD, Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness.

A new video podcasts section for Apple TV won’t go behind the subscription paywall.
Apple’s streaming service will soon have a video podcasts section, the New York Times reports. It will start testing the feature in a developer release today, so expect a new update for iOS 27.3 beta testers to roll out in a few hours. Once it rolls out fully, the new video podcasts section will be available to everyone using an Apple TV device or app on all supported platforms.
The expansion follows other streaming services’ push into podcasts. Netflix announced it was adding video podcasts to its platform last year, and debuted its first original video podcast series in January. Hulu and Disney Plus also offer podcasts, including a mix of companion podcasts for their shows and licensed podcasts like We’re Here to Help , hosted by Jake Johnson and Gareth Reynolds. Spotify has had support for video podcasts for several years now, and last year expanded them to its tvOS app . YouTube’s TV app has long been an option for watching podcasts, as well.
Besides bringing its video podcasts to more screens, Apple is also planning to add more video podcasts to its regular Podcasts app, according to the Times . Apple added support for switching between audio and video podcasts in its iOS Podcasts app earlier this year, and added video podcasts on the tvOS Podcasts app in September.

İtalya Veri Koruma Kurumu Garante, Meta'ya 805 milyon euro idari para cezası kesti. Kurum, Facebook'un Android uygulamasının İtalyan kullanıcıların telefonlarındaki fotoğraf, video ve metaverilere özel bir onay almadan eriştiğini tespit etti. Ceza, Meta'nın küresel cirosunun yaklaşık yüzde 0,47'sine denk geliyor.
Soruşturmaya konu olan özellik, Facebook'un Android uygulamasında 2023 'ten beri bulunan 'Facebook'ta gezinirken galeriden öneriler al' seçeneği. Telefondaki fotoğraf ve videoları tarayıp paylaşım önerisi olarak sunuyor. Garante'nin tespitine göre özellik varsayılan olarak açıktı ve uygulama, kullanıcıdan bu iş için ayrıca onay istemeden galerideki fotoğraflara, videolara ve bunların metaverilerine ulaştı.
Kurum, sorunun bir kısmını izin yapısında buldu. Uygulama tek bir izinle birden fazla işlevi kapsıyordu ve diğer özelliklere dair genel bir bilgilendirme, galeri önerilerinin de devreye girdiğini açıkça göstermiyordu. Soruşturma, Temmuz 2025'te Bolzano merkezli tüketici derneği Centro Tutela Consumatori Utenti'nin şikâyetiyle başladı ve Garante'nin kendi teknik analiziyle ilerledi.
Garante, ihlali İtalya 'nın Gizlilik Yasası'nın 122. maddesine, yani AB 'nin e-Gizlilik Direktifi'ni yürürlüğe koyan hükme dayandırdı. Karara göre telefonda saklanan verilere her erişim için özgür ve bilgilendirilmiş bir onay gerekiyor. Veri bir yere gönderilmiş ya da kullanıcı zarar görmüş olması aranmıyor. Kurum, yasanın 'akıllı telefonu kişinin özel alanının bir parçası olarak koruduğunu' vurguladı.
Cezanın hesabında yaklaşık 20 milyon Android kullanıcısı, ihlalin süresi, Meta hakkında 2019'da verilmiş önceki bir karar ve soruşturma sırasında gösterilen sınırlı iş birliği ağırlaştırıcı unsur olarak sayıldı. Şikâyetten sonra yapılan değişiklikler hafifletici bulundu, ancak kurum bunları geç ve yalnızca uygulamayı güncelleyen kullanıcılarla sınırlı olarak değerlendirdi. Meta, dosyayı İrlanda'daki veri koruma otoritesinin görmesi gerektiğini savundu. Garante, e-Gizlilik kurallarında tek duraktan işlem mekanizması bulunmadığı için bu itirazı reddetti.
Para cezasının yanında Meta'ya bir dizi yükümlülük de getirildi. Şirket 30 gün içinde başlattığı çalışmaları Garante'ye bildirecek, 60 gün içinde galeri özelliği için ayrı ve özel bir onay talebi sunacak. Bu talepte özelliğin ne yaptığı, galeriye eriştiği ve nasıl kapatılabileceği anlatılacak. Özellik, daha önce izin vermiş kullanıcılar dahil herkes için varsayılan olarak kapalı tutulacak. 90. günde ise alınan önlemlere dair ikinci bir rapor verilecek.
60 günlük süre kaçırılırsa özellik, geçerli bir onay olmadan hiçbir kullanıcı için açılamayacak. Garante ayrıca Meta'nın bu yıl devreye aldığı, galeri içeriğinin bulutta işlenmesine izin veren yeni özelliği ayrı bir inceleme konusu yapacak. Yapay zeka eğitimi için kullanılıp kullanılmadığı bu soruşturmanın kapsamında değildi; Meta böyle bir kullanımı reddediyor.
Meta, Garante'nin olgulara dair değerlendirmesine ve mevzuatı uygulayışına net biçimde katılmadığını belirtti. Şirket cezayı 'orantısız' olarak nitelendirdi ve karara karşı itiraz yoluna gideceğini duyurdu. Meta'ya göre özellik, ancak kullanıcı cihazında gerekli izni verdikten sonra çalışıyor ve bu izin ayarlardan istenen zaman değiştirilebiliyor.
Dosyanın bundan sonrası iki başlıkta ilerleyecek: Meta'nın itiraz başvurusu ve Ocak 2027'nin ortasında dolacak 60 günlük süre. Konuyla ilgili Fransız haber ajansı AFP'nin paylaşımı şöyle:

Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people.
The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.
The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys.
Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor’s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues.
Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours.
“At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.”
The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week .

Inside the Friday the 13th telecommunications breakdown that stranded 1.5 million flyers, and the chaotic briefings that fueled conspiracy theories instead of public trust.
Thirty minutes outside Atlanta, the pilot got on the intercom to announce that something was wrong.
A communications issue with the Federal Aviation Administration was cascading across the country. The pilot didn’t offer much detail except to say that the issue might affect gate access and connecting flights.
For Amanda Khera, the timing couldn’t be worse. Her family vacation to a small island off the coast of Belize had already turned into a medical scare when her 22-month-old son Rio developed a high fever and had to be rushed to a local clinic. Exhausted, they were trying to get home to Virginia Beach, Virginia, to see his pediatrician and rest in their own bed. First, they had to connect through Atlanta.
“It was honestly pretty scary,” Khera said. “We didn’t know if the pilot was flying blind without any access to the control towers, or if planes would run into each other.”
“We didn’t know if the pilot was flying blind without any access to the control towers, or if planes would run into each other.”
She had every right to be scared. She didn’t know what was going on in the cockpit or on the ground. She had no idea that pilots are trained to follow strict procedures that minimize safety risks during major air traffic control outages. All she knew was that several recent incidents , including a midair collision over Reagan National Airport in 2025 that killed 67 people, have called into question the safety of America’s skies. So she spent the rest of the descent looking out the window for nearby aircraft.
Her flight landed safely. But she deplaned into a terminal frozen in place. More than 600 flights out of Atlanta , including their connection to Norfolk, had been canceled. And no one knew when they would be able to take off because every flight across the United States had been grounded.
On Friday, November 13, the nation’s air traffic control system began to fail. Around 3:15PM ET, pilots and air traffic controllers in the Midwest started reporting difficulty communicating with each other over the radio.
“We’re 11,000 [feet] over Grand Rapids airport, about nine miles to the west,” said the pilot of Allegiant Flight 547, his transmission already becoming garbled . “Unable to get… contact… approach on any [frequency].”
Four minutes later, controllers at Quad Cities Airport in Moline, Illinois, reported similar issues across the region.
“We’re dealing with some communication issues on a larger scale than we initially anticipated,” said one. “It sounds like Chicago Approach is going ATC zero, so it might be worse than we initially thought. We thought it was just here.”
With communication outages spreading around the country, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop at 3:54PM ET “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” From that moment on, no airplanes were allowed to take off in US airspace.
“Just a heads up, we went in a national ground stop,” said a controller in Seattle.
“Are you saying national as in Reagan National,” asked one United pilot, “or national in the whole country?”
“Across all en route facilities, they’re having communication issues.”
Like so many of the safety incidents that have plagued the air traffic control system over the last few years, this latest failure began with a fragile and outdated piece of FAA infrastructure. In this case, according to the agency , the faulty system was the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure, or FTI .
Built by defense giant L3Harris in the early 2000s, FTI is the data backbone of the entire air traffic control system. It links more than 4,400 aviation facilities and carries the voice and radar data controllers rely on to keep planes separated, bridging the gap between the FAA’s legacy phone-based transmission systems and modern,Internet Protocol-based ones.
FTI is scheduled to be replaced in 2028 . Until then, L3Harris must make incremental upgrades to keep FTI operational.
“We’re dealing with some communication issues on a larger scale than we initially anticipated.”
One of these upgrades accidentally brought down the entire system, according to The Wall Street Journal . Early in the day, L3Harris contractors replaced an old wired telephone switch with a new wireless data router at the FAA radio facility in El Dorado, Arkansas. Once activated, however, the router began to flood the network with hundreds of connection attempts every second.
This may have added enough extra load to the system to degrade the whole network’s performance, according to I-Hong Hou, professor of electrical and computer engineering at Texas A&M University.
Hou explained that telecom networks break pieces of information — radio transmissions or radar coordinates, for example — into data packets small enough to be transmitted over the network and reassembled at the other end.
“When the network is degraded, it may start to lose a small portion of packets,” Hou said. “Since you need all packets to reassemble the data feed, just dropping one out of 10 packets may cause your feed to completely stop.”
Most modern communications apps are built to compensate for packet loss. FaceTime, for example, will blur the video or switch to audio-only to preserve the connection.
“Many NAS [National Air Space] applications … require a highly reliable synchronization source with exceptional stability,” according to FAA technical documentation , which warns that instability may cause widespread failure of critical systems.
FAA technicians believe the El Dorado router’s repeated connection attempts created enough instability within the FTI to cut off radio and radar feeds to 17 of the FAA’s 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers and several Terminal Radar Approach Controls .
“We sometimes call this a cascading failure, meaning that one failed device can cause nearby devices to fail, and so on,” explained Hou.
“We sometimes call this a cascading failure, meaning that one failed device can cause nearby devices to fail, and so on.”
L3Harris’s contractors isolated the malfunctioning router and another one at a nearby radar facility in Amarillo, Texas. Once those two routers were taken offline, the network began to stabilize once again .
Four and a half hours later, at 8:15PM ET, the FAA lifted the ground stop. It was the nation’s longest since 9/11, spurring airlines to cancel more than 13,000 flights and delay more than 25,000 more through the weekend, according to FlightAware . And more than 1.5 million passengers were stranded.
Faulty technology created the crisis. The FAA’s hamfisted attempts to reassure the public that everything was okay made the situation worse.
For six hours after the ground stop began, the FAA did not provide any public updates except for a terse, 31-word press release and a single X post . Finally, at 11:30PM ET, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin held a press conference to explain the day’s events.
Instead of providing clarity, however, they issued confusing and sometimes even contradictory statements. Mullin opened the conference with a joke (“Welcome to Friday the 13th, right?”) before confidently declaring that “there is no cyberattack.” Instead, he appeared to blame the outage on the FAA’s modernization project.
“As Secretary Duffy and FAA was going in and putting patches into the system, they were putting new equipment and new technology, and that new equipment and technology was just overwhelming the older system,” said Mullin.
Mullin’s remark appeared to surprise Duffy, who looked at the ground and shook his head. Mullin later walked the statement back after a reporter’s follow-up question, admitting that “there’s nothing completely certain right now.”

Dig deep enough, and the temperature of the ground remains steady year round, a fun trivia fact that has the potential to improve efficiency and slash costs for heating and cooling across the country.
Geothermal heat pumps, which use the ground as a heat source in winter and heat sink in summer, have been around for decades, but they’re underutilized. Just a fraction of all buildings in the U.S. use them in part because it’s expensive to drill into the earth. But one startup, Bedrock Energy , says its AI-directed rigs can slash drilling times by up to 80%, significantly reducing costs.
That time savings recently helped Bedrock raise a new $24 million funding round, the startup told TechCrunch. Previously, it raised a $12 million Series A in 2025 and an $8.5 million seed round in 2023.
Bedrock has focused mostly on commercial properties to date, since they benefit from deep, accurate boreholes which maximize the use of their small footprints. But the startup has also been talking with data center developers, Joselyn Lai, co-founder and CEO of Bedrock Energy, told TechCrunch. Some might use it for cooling server racks, but others are interested in the technology’s flat load profile — deploying it on neighboring properties can open up significant capacity on the grid.
“We had someone in Michigan say, if we could free up a few megawatts, I think we might be able to operate that many months or even a year earlier,” Lai said. “A year of revenue for a data center is very meaningful.”
Bedrock says its modernized approach to shallow geothermal drilling — up to 1,0000 feet or so — sets it apart. Most geothermal heat pump drillers use rigs that are similar to those used for water wells. They work fine, but they’re crude instruments.
Instead, Bedrock uses directional drilling techniques borrowed from the oil and gas industry, guiding them using its own models of the subsurface. That combination allows them to optimize drilling and placement, the company says, helping to ensure performance and longevity. Sensors in the boreholes help to refine those models.
The startup currently operates in Utah, Colorado, New York, Alberta, and its home state of Texas, and the new round will help the company expand into New England, New Jersey, the upper Midwest, and additional states in the West, Lai said.
To power that expansion, Bedrock will add more rigs to its fleet to serve customers in those regions. Currently, it has drilled boreholes in nine sites, and it has secured payments from new customers in anticipation of drilling in the next year or two, she added.
Once up and running, a geothermal heat pump requires far less maintenance than traditional HVAC systems. “You only have to install it once and then it works for a very long time, which is very good for infrastructure from a financial perspective,” Lai said.
The new round was led by Clean Energy Ventures and Clearvision Ventures with participation from GVP Climate, Susquehanna Sustainable Investments, Catalytic Capital for Climate and Health by Temasek Trust, MUUS, Great Wave Ventures, Autodesk Foundation, Titanium Ventures, Energy Impact Partners, Wireframe Ventures, Elemental Impact, and SFV Capital.

Şirket, sağlık alanında yapay zeka çözümleri geliştiren OpenEvidence ile iş birliği yaparak bu araştırma için özel bir uygulama hazırladı. 12 aydan uzun sürmesi planlanan araştırmaya 200 bine kadar katılımcının dahil edilmesi hedefleniyor.

Bu kapsamda geliştirilen uygulama, ChatGPT ve Claude gibi sohbet botlarına benzer şekilde kullanıcıların sağlıkla ilgili sorularını yanıtlıyor. Ancak uygulamanın yanıtları The New England Journal of Medicine , Journal of the American Medical Association ve Nature gibi yayınlarda yer alan klinik verilere dayanıyor.
Kullanıcılar, aldıkları yanıtları puanlayabiliyor ve geri bildirimde bulunabiliyor. Ayrıca araştırmaya katılanlardan her ay anketleri yanıtlamaları isteniyor. Katılımcılar, daha kişiselleştirilmiş yanıtlar alabilmek için dinlenme kalp atış hızı, fiziksel aktivite, uyku ve laboratuvar sonuçları gibi Apple HealthKit verilerini de uygulamayla paylaşabiliyor. Uygulama, kullanıcıların doktor randevularına hazırlanmasına yardımcı olmanın yanı sıra endişe verici sağlık sorunlarında ilgili uzmanlara yönlendirme yapabiliyor.

Apple, araştırma kapsamında toplanan verilerin güvenli bir üçüncü taraf bulut sağlayıcısına gönderilmeden önce anonim hale getirileceğini ve herhangi bir yapay zeka modelini eğitmek için kullanılmayacağını belirtiyor. Audible is introducing an AI-assisted synopsis feature that’s designed to help users determine whether they’ll enjoy an audiobook before they jump in and start listening to it. The new audio discovery feature combines audiobook samples, AI overviews, and author commentary to give users more information before choosing their next story, in addition to recommended audiobook collections that are personalized to individual listening tastes.
Audio discovery provides a soundbite synopsis, with the aim of preventing Audible users from having to research titles on other platforms. The feature plays users a snippet of the audiobook and a brief AI-generated overview including its themes and listener reactions, drawing from reviews and other publicly available data. It can also include commentary from an author or Audible editor, which is pulled directly from past Audible interviews.
“Picking your next listen should feel like getting a tip from a friend. With audio discovery, you’ll get a quick audio take on why the title might be right for you, from our editors, fellow listeners, or even the author,” Audible chief product officer Andy Tsao said in the announcement. “Some of the best listening experiences are those rare finds or hidden gems, and we want to make those great discoveries happen more often and more easily.”
Audio discovery is rolling out on select English-language titles in the US, with plans to eventually expand to other regions.
Audible is also using AI to personalize audiobook collections around users’ listening tastes, in an effort to make titles that don’t appear on best-selling lists easier to discover. Like audio discovery, these personalized collections are rolling out to customers in the US, and also include commentary from Audible’s editors.
These are the latest AI-powered features that Audible is introducing in an effort to attract new users and fend off growing competition from rival platforms like Spotify . As part of this update, Audible is also expanding two beta features: Ask a Question , which allows users to ask AI about characters, plot points, references, and more; and Recaps, which provides spoiler-free audio summaries of what the user has already listened to. These are now available for a “select set” of additional English-language titles in the US, according to Audible, with a broader rollout planned to start in December.

Success in geothermal energy is guided by two basic goals — drill fast and drill deep. Hit both targets, and geothermal startups have a good chance at being cheaper than nearly every other source on the electrical grid.
But while the goals might be straightforward, they’re anything but easy. Drilling fast generates heat, which damages equipment, and so does drilling deep.
Those two foes are what led Mazama Energy to develop a new technology, called Carbon Chill, that uses carbon dioxide to cool the drill bit and bring cuttings to the surface. The technology will not only let the company drill deeper, but also faster. The startup gave TechCrunch an exclusive look at Carbon Chill.
“Our rate of penetration increased 20% over the already very high rates we were achieving,” Sriram Vasantharajan, co-founder and CEO of Mazama Energy, told TechCrunch.
Speed has other advantages in geothermal. Drilling represents about 25% to 30% of the total cost of building a power plant, so reducing drill time can bring costs down significantly.
If geothermal startups succeed in drilling faster and cheaper, they stand to help reshape the grid in the 2030s. Hyperscalers are already planning the facilities that will enter operation at the end of the decade.
Mazama has been working on the problem for years now. In October 2025, the Khosla-backed startup said it had drilled a well in Oregon that reached 629˚ F (331˚ C), and a more recent well has surpassed 700˚ C, Vasantharajan said. In September, the startup raised $135 million in a round led by Centaurus Capital and Doerr Capital.
Mazama hopes that its new carbon dioxide-based cooling technology will help it prove that geothermal energy from super-hot rock is a viable contender in the electricity market.
Already companies like Google and Meta have started to explore the use of geothermal energy, in part because the potential is enormous: a report from the National Laboratory of the Rockies said that geothermal could generate between 26.5 to 57 terawatts of electricity in the U.S. alone. If just 10% of the conservative estimate were developed, it would more than double the U.S.’s peak generating capacity.
Geothermal experts have identified super-hot rock — in which temperatures exceed 752˚ F (400˚ C) — as a promising way to improve the performance of individual wells. At those temperatures, water turns “supercritical,” a gaseous-like liquid state which carries five to ten times more energy than water from traditional geothermal wells. By harvesting more energy from a each well, developers have to drill fewer of them, bringing costs down.
Accessing that heat can be challenging for traditional drilling methods. Most geothermal drillers use “mud” — a combination of water and other compounds to keep the bit cool and clear cuttings from the borehole. But mud can only bring temperatures down so much. Eventually, they become so hot that electronics in the drill bit, which help keep it on course, start to fail.
High temperature-rated electronics exist, but they’d be cost prohibitive, Vasantharajan said.
Instead of mud, Mazama injects liquid carbon dioxide down the center of its drill string. As it is travels deeper, it gets heated by the rock around it, which turns it supercritical, too. Then, just before it reaches the drill head, Mazama has it flow through a valve that looks a lot like a rocket nozzle. As the gas expands, it escapes through the cone-shaped nozzle, rapidly cools, absorbing heat from the electronics and the drill bit.
“I look at [carbon dioxide cooling] as a binary,” he said. “Without such technologies, I am, today, not able to drill these horizontal wells at super hot rock temperatures.”
That capital injection will help Mazama drill more wells deeper. By next year, Vasantharajan said his company hopes to complete a single well that’s capable of generating up to 15 megawatts of electricity.
“What was just a dream or a quest, I can tell you with confidence is now a promise,” he said. “We see a path towards this commercial super-hot rock geothermal.”

Özgür Özel'in yeniden genel başkan seçildiği kurultayda Yeni Parti yönetimini de seçti. 160 kişilik Parti Meclisi'nde kimler yer aldı?
Yeni Parti , ilk kurultayını Parti Meclisi ve Yüksek Disiplin Kurulu seçimleriyle tamamlarken, Parti Meclisi alınan yeni kararla 160 kişiden oluştu.
Mutlak butlan kararı ile CHP'de genel başkanlıktan alınan Özgür Özel liderliğinde kurulan Yeni Parti 'nin ilk olağan kurultayı hafta sonu Ankara'da gerçekleştirildi.
Kurultayın ikinci günü Parti Meclisi (PM) ve Yüksek Disiplin Kurulu (YDK) seçimleriyle sona erdi. Delegeler, Özel'in hazırladığı 160 kişilik PM ve 15 kişilik YDK listelerini onayladı.
"Türkiye Yenileniyor" sloganıyla Ankara Spor Salonu'nda düzenlenen kurultayda, kayıtlı 1202 delegeden 1116'sı yönetim organlarının seçimi için oy kullandı. Sandıklardan çıkan 1098 oy geçerli sayıldı.
Özgür Özel 'in blok listesindeki bütün adaylar seçilirken 22 isim 1092 oyla en yüksek oyu paylaştı.
Kurultayın ilk gününde tek aday olarak genel başkanlık seçimine giren Özel, 1154 geçerli oyun tamamını almıştı. Delegeler, ilk gün çalışma ve hesap raporlarıyla Kurultay Sonuç Bildirgesi'ni de kabul etmişti.
Kurultayın ikinci gününde yönetim kadrosuna ilişkin en dikkat çekici gelişmelerden biri PM'nin genişletilmesi oldu.
Kurucular Kurulu, kurultay öncesinde 80 kişilik PM'nin üye sayısını bir dönem için 150'ye yükseltmişti. Kurucular Kurulu'nun verdiği yetki ile bu sayı 10 kişi daha artırıldı.
Parti yönetimi, artışın gerekçesini Politika Geliştirme Grubu'na yönelik yoğun talep olarak açıkladı. Yeni yapılanmaya göre PM, 80 kişilik yasama grubu, 40 kişilik örgüt grubu ve 40 kişilik politika geliştirme grubundan oluşuyor.
Yeni PM'de mevcut milletvekilleri ve parti yöneticilerinin yanı sıra ekonomi, dış politika, hukuk, sağlık ve eğitim alanlarından isimler yer aldı.
Selin Sayek Böke, Ümit Özlale, Yalçın Karatepe, Serkan Özcan, Kerim Rota, Güldem Atabay ve Öner Günçavdı ekonomi kadrosunda yer alan isimler oldu.

Bilim insanı Cem Say, gıda mühendisi Bülent Şık ve Eğitim-İş Genel Başkanı Kadem Özbay da yönetime yeni giren isimler arasında yer aldı.
Demokrasi, adalet ve özgürlükler alanındaki ekipte Gül Çiftçi, İlhan Cihaner, Şule Özsoy Boyunsuz, Gökçe Gökçen, Bahadır Erdem ve Barış Övgün görevlerini korudu. Avukatlar Ekrem Baki ve Egemen Gürcün, akademisyenler Oğuz Kurdoğlu ve Burak Cop ile eski Devlet Bakanı Ahat Andican da bu kadroya dahil oldu.
Sosyal politika ve sağlık kadrosuna katılan isimler ise eski Türk Tabipleri Birliği Merkez Konseyi Başkanı Prof. Dr. Sinan Adıyaman, Prof. Dr. Şengül Hablemitoğlu ve eski Türk Eczacıları Birliği Başkanı Arman Üney oldu. Sosyal politika ve sağlık alanındaki kadroda Aylin Yaman, Kayıhan Pala, Aylin Nazlıaka, Emine Uçak Erdoğan ve Murat Arslan ise yerlerini korudu.
Özel, ikinci gün oyunu kullandıktan sonra gazetecilere yaptığı açıklamada, mahallelerden başlayarak ilçe ve il örgütleriyle devam eden kuruluş sürecini kurultayla tamamladıklarını söyleyerek, yeni kadroların iktidara hazırlık çalışmalarını yürüteceğini belirtti.
Özel, PM'nin genişlemesini farklı alanlardan uzmanların katkı sunma isteğiyle açıkladı. Özel, sosyal politika, sağlık, tarım ve milli savunma alanlarında uzman ekipler oluşturduklarını belirtti. Özel, Öner Günçavdı ve Murat Kubilay'ın da katılımıyla Ekonomi Eşgüdüm Konseyi'nin 14 kişiye ulaştığını kaydetti.
Ekonomi alanında çalışacak olan ekibin yeni kalkınma modeli, vergi reformu, ekonomik krizin aşılması ve gelir dağılımında adaletin sağlanması üzerinde çalışacağını söyleyen Özel, ekonomi kadrosunun görevini "Ekmeği nasıl büyütüp nasıl hakça paylaşacağımızı anlatacağımız kadrolarımız olacak" sözleriyle anlattı.
Özel, uzman grubunu başlangıçta 30 kişi olarak tasarladıklarını, görev tekliflerine olumlu yanıtlar ve dışarıdan gelen talepler üzerine bu sayıyı 40'a yükselttiklerini söyledi. Özel, üç uzmanı da memleketlerinden aday göstererek toplam uzman sayısını 43'e çıkardıklarını belirtti. Özel, geçmişte PM'deki eleştirileri azaltmak amacıyla üye sayısının düşürülmesine yönelik sözler duyduğunu hatırlatarak yeni yapılanmada daha geniş katılımı savundu.
Kurultayda kabul edilen ve Genel Sekreter Yunus Emre'nin okuduğu Kuruluş Kurultayı Bildirgesi, partinin yönetim sistemi, ekonomi ve temel haklar alanındaki hedeflerini ortaya koydu.
Yeni Parti, bildirgede siyasi gücün, ekonomik zenginliğin ve kamu kaynaklarının iktidara yakın bir azınlıkta toplandığını savunarak Türkiye'nin ihtiyacının yalnızca iktidar değişikliğiyle sınırlı olmadığını belirtti.
Parti, güçlü bir Meclis, kuvvetler ayrılığı, bağımsız yargı ve demokratik denetime dayalı parlamenter sisteme dönüşü hedefleri arasında sıraladı. Yeni Parti, seçilmiş yerel yöneticilerin yerine kayyım atanmasına son verilmesini ve kadınlara yönelik şiddetle mücadelede İstanbul Sözleşmesi'nin uygulanmasını da taahhüt etti.
Yeni Parti, ekonomi alanında emeğin milli gelirden aldığı payın artırılmasını, vergi reformunu ve sosyal devletin güçlendirilmesini hedeflediğini açıkladı. Parti, dış politikada Avrupa Birliği üyeliği hedefini sürdüreceğini, NATO üyeliğinin sunduğu imkânlardan yararlanacağını, Rusya ve Çin'le ilişkileri ise karşılıklı yarar temelinde geliştireceğini belirtti.
Parti, iktidara hazırlık kapsamında uygulamaya hazır programlarını, sorumluluk üstlenecek kadrolarını ve politikalarının finansman kaynaklarını kamuoyuna sunacağını bildirdi. Yeni Parti, bildirgede bu yaklaşımını "Türkiye'yi yönetme hazırlıklarımızı somut hedeflere, açık takvimlere ve ölçülebilir sonuçlara dayandıracağız" sözleriyle ifade etti.
Özel'in ikinci günkü açıklamalarında fon krizi de gündeme geldi.
Parti kurmaylarının sekiz ana dosyada teyit çalışmalarını tamamladığını belirten Özel, "Tahmin ediyorum bu haftadan itibaren o dosyaları ayrı ayrı açıklayacaklar. Tüm yönleriyle teyit edilmiş bilgilerle, içinde siyasetçi olur, şirket olur, arkadaşlarımız açıklayacak. Listeyi açıklamamak lekelenmemesi gereken herkesi lekeliyor" diye konuştu.
Özel, açıklamanın ne zaman yapılacağı ile ilgili olarak ise partili yetkililere teyit almadan isim açıklamamaları talimatını verdiğini söyleyerek, şöyle konuştu:
"Ama çok sayıda isimden bahsediliyor. Arkadaşlarımız teyit aldıkları isimleri açıklayacaklar. Açıklanana kadar spekülasyon yapacak bir tarihten kaçınıyorum."

Pro-government forces said troops were being moved to defend the interim capital, Aden (file photo)
Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia say they are redeploying troops to defend the country's interim capital, Aden, following weeks of intensified fighting with the Iran-backed Houthi movement.
The Southern Armed Forces said it was withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, at the southern end of the Red Sea, to reinforce positions around Aden and neighbouring areas.
Houthi-run media say the movement has taken control of the evacuated territory. Saudi Arabia has not commented.
The shift ends a weeks-long offensive to try to secure the area near the key shipping route which the Houthis seized in a surprise offensive in September.
Pro-government forces said they had "secured" the strait in early October as they sought to retake crucial ground from the Houthis. The Iran-backed fighters said they had captured areas including Perim Island at the mouth of the strait and the strategic port city of Mokha a month prior.
But the Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces fighting on behalf of Yemen's internationally recognised government said on Sunday they were withdrawing to reinforce troops elsewhere, with the southern city of Aden a "priority".
It said troops were being withdrawn "from Dhubab Airport and the Bab al-Mandab area" with the aim of "strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats".
"This step is driven by the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and neighbouring governorates, reinforcing the front lines and addressing existing threats."
The Houthis said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway when they captured territory overlooking it, but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.
However, the seizure contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.
A UN Human Rights spokesperson, Ravina Shamdasani, urged all parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure.
She noted that since the escalation of fighting in August, more than 60% of documented civilian casualties were women and children.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Aden in recent weeks, including an assault on 15 October that targeted the presidential palace, killing five and injuring 16.
Saudi Arabia responded with hundreds of air strikes, while the Houthis launched hundreds of drones and missiles at its cities and infrastructure.
The UN has estimated that nearly 330,000 people have been displaced in Yemen as the fighting has since escalated. Hundreds of people are reported to have been killed.
Yemenis flee across Red Sea as Houthis and Saudi-backed forces escalate war
Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from its capital, Sanaa.
The conflict escalated in 2015 after a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.
A four-year informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

The point-to-point driver assist is coming to the US and Germany in 2027.
SAN FRANCISCO—When Ars first drove the new Mercedes-Benz CLA last year , the automaker also gave us a sneak preview of its next driver assist. Called Drive Assist Pro, it’s for collaborative partially assisted driving, and from the passenger seat at the time, the demo was impressive . Now the automaker is getting ready to start rolling out Drive Assist Pro to customers with cars running the new MB.OS operating system here in the US and in Germany, and it let us have some time behind the wheel.
While most automakers want a reputation associated with safety, Mercedes has long used passive and active technology to do so in its products. It was one of the first OEMs to introduce airbags, then a decade later started adding active safety systems like antilock brakes, electronic stability control, and adaptive cruise control. And so, by giving the car’s electronics the ability to control the brakes, and throttle, we arrive at the first level of assisted driving—called “level 1” in automotive engineerspeak.
“Level 2” assisted driving, where the car also controls the steering as well as the acceleration and braking, got famous with Tesla Autopilot. But the first lane-keeping assists predate it by almost a decade in passenger cars, when Toyota introduced a system in 2004. The human driver behind the wheel is still in charge, responsible for situational awareness (and anything that arises from a lack thereof), with the idea that long drives become less tiring and a little more effortless when the car does the boring job of keeping a constant speed or a constant distance to the car ahead and between the white lines.
The next step, numerically at least, should be level 3, where we move from assisted driving to partially automated driving; here the car takes over the task of driving fully under some circumstances, like heavy traffic . But that’s getting ahead of ourselves—the main developments over the past few years have been the inelegantly named “L2+” systems that combine more advanced driver monitoring with a higher degree of assistance, usually on geofenced highways.
General Motors’ Super Cruise was the first of these, allowing hands-free operation as long as the car can tell the driver has their eyes on the road. Now many automakers offer something similar: Ford has Bluecruise, BMW has Highway Assistant, and Mercedes is about to add a hands-free highway assist next spring to its MB. Drive Assist system, which will be standard on the 2027 S-Class and AMG GT 4-Door Coupe and an option on the 2027 CLA, GLB, C-Class, GLC, and GLE.
I tested that system while in San Francisco in a 2027 S-Class, and it’s competent within its operational design domain. The user interface is a little more subtle than Super Cruise’s big green LED in the steering wheel; instead, the icon on the dash changes, with the hands on the steering wheel going from green to grey when it’s safe to remove them. Like other systems, MB. Drive Assist has been programmed to make automatic lane changes if the car decides that’s going to be quicker—these can be canceled with the turn signal or simply by resisting the car steering into the next lane.
MB. Drive Assist Pro takes that idea and brings it to lower speeds and much more complex traffic situations—“level 2++” (we really need to stop letting engineers name things). Instead of hands on the green steering wheel icon, there’s a large green arrowhead, showing you’re in point-to-point mode—compared to the various configurations of the highway assist, I found this much less likely to engender mode confusion. (Did the green hands mean I could take my hands on or off the wheel? On, but see what I mean?)
The driving behavior was about exactly as cautious as I would want on surface streets. The electric GLC was as smooth accelerating and braking as the entirely autonomous Waymo robotaxi I rode in the day before, and the car’s electronic brain was able to safely pass double-parked cars—waiting patiently for an oncoming bus first—and stopped for stop signs, red lights, and pedestrians on crosswalks (while making a left turn at the time). The system is collaborative—steering or accelerating won’t end the automation, but unlike BMW’s new iX5 , any use of the brake will turn it off.
Some customers in Germany and California will be part of an early access program for Drive Assist Pro from next month, with a wider rollout in the first half of 2027 for model year 2026 CLAs, as well as the model year 2027 CLA, GLC Electric, GLE, GLS, and S-Class, and more coming in model year 2028. (The system is already live in China.)
The unifying factor is the MB.OS, the automaker’s latest operating system . Like other automakers, Mercedes has embraced the software-defined vehicle paradigm, replacing dozens or even hundreds of discrete ECUs with a handful of powerful domain controller computers that oversee vehicle dynamics, occupant comfort, infotainment, and automation.
Drive Assist Pro combines a mix of 10 cameras, five radars, and 12 ultrasonic sensors, all stitched together by a domain controller that uses Nvidia’s Orin processors. I’m told that in China, cars are now advertised with processor and RAM specs rather than boring information like range or performance: In that spirit, Mercedes says it can deliver 254 tera operations per second, uses a 2.5 Gbit ethernet network, and has more than 70GB of RAM.
The driving decisions are made by Nvidia’s Alpamayo end-to-end tokenized stack that picks your driving trajectory, with a rules-based system running alongside as a safety check. That’s reassuring, as is the knowledge that Nvidia’s stack has been certified by Germany’s TUV, which takes a less lackadaisical approach to safety than the current incarnation of the US Department of Transportation.

Romelu Lukaku scored three goals for Belgium at the World Cup this summer
Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, saying he has "enjoyed every single moment" of playing for Belgium.
Fenerbahce striker Lukaku, 33, made his international debut in 2010 and is Belgium's all-time leading men's goalscorer with 94 goals in 135 appearances.
He is the fifth highest men's international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and leader Cristiano Ronaldo, who has scored 146.
Lukaku scored eight goals across four World Cups, including in the run to the quarter-finals at this summer's tournament, and a total of six goals at three European Championships.
Writing on Instagram, , external the former Everton, Chelsea and Manchester United forward thanked his team-mates and coaches "for pushing and trusting me to help the team" during his 16 years with the national side.
He missed Belgium's Nations League win over Turkey last week with a hip injury and was an unused substitute on Sunday as they qualified for the last eight of the competition by beating Italy 4-1.
"These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team... I went through every emotion possible," Lukaku wrote.
"To the Belgium fans thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in four World Cups and three European Championships.
"I will never forget those moments. I'm at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable. I'm grateful."
In 2023, Lukaku scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, breaking the record for goals scored by a player in a European Championship qualifying campaign.
His Belgium team-mate Kevin de Bruyne posted an image of himself with Lukaku , external on Instagram adding: "There are no words to describe what you've meant to me and our country!"

Saudi Arabia has removed the commander of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, state media said Monday, as the Iran-backed rebels advanced on the temporary capital of Aden. The shake up comes after Houthi forces took territory on Yemen's southern coast and Saudi-backed forces fell back to defend the capital.
Saudi authorities on Monday dismissed the commander of the coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen , as the Iran-backed group advanced towards the seat of government in Aden.
"Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad bin Abdulaziz al-Salman is appointed as advisor for military affairs to the Minister of Defence," the official Saudi Press Agency said, citing a royal decree, naming chief of staff General Fayyad bin Hamed bin Ruqad al-Ruwaili as the coalition's new commander.
The news comes as Houthi fighters have seized territory on Yemen's southern coast after Saudi-backed government forces fell back to defend Aden, military sources said on Monday, as residents expressed fear of further advances by the Iran-allied group towards the city.
Read more Yemen's Houthis advance on Aden as government forces retreat to defend their capital
The Houthis have seized swathes of territory from Yemen's internationally recognised government since the US-Iran conflict reignited the frozen civil war this ‌summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group.
Following a counter-attack by its forces in ⁠October, the Yemeni government said on Sunday it was withdrawing from areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global shipping artery, to focus on defending the southern port city of ‌Aden.
Five Yemeni military people said on Monday that Houthi fighters had advanced to the southern coastal area ⁠of Khor Omairh, some 100km (62 miles) west of Aden, and were 25km (16 miles) from government lines at Qawah, also on the coast.
Residents of Aden said government security forces had set up more checkpoints and were carrying out identity checks in the city, the government's seat of power since the Houthis ‌took Sanaa in 2014.
"Food supplies are available, and so is fuel. However, people are worried about the retreat of government forces and the possibility of fighting drawing closer to Aden," government employee Amin Mahmoud told Reuters by phone from the city.
The withdrawal marks a big setback ‌in the Saudi-backed campaign against the Houthis, who have been firing ballistic missiles at Saudi airports and oil facilities since the Yemen war restarted.

The Yemeni government's focus is to secure Aden and the province of Lahj, three government sources said.
Government forces were redeploying and reorganising along front lines to prepare for the recapture of areas seized by the Houthis, the sources said.
Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping have enhanced Iran 's position in the wider Middle East conflict launched by the United States and Israel in February.
"There is a serious threat to Aden because they are getting closer and closer. It is a major setback. The government was aiming to recapture Sanaa, but now they are defending Aden," said Mohammed Al-Qadhi, a political and conflict analyst.
One of the major problems facing government forces is their fragmented state, he said, adding that the Houthis were benefiting from "an accumulation of years of disagreements and infighting" on the government side.
Yemen's civil war had been dormant since 2022 until it reignited this summer as a spillover of the Iran war.
The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the Red Sea and the Bab ⁠el-Mandeb Strait that controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country's third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.
Saudi-backed government forces ⁠rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, in an offensive last month. But they were unable to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

Houthi fighters are edging closer to the temporary capital following a sudden withdrawal of government-aligned forces from the Bab al-Mandeb area.
Forces aligned with the internationally recognised Yemeni government face a potentially catastrophic situation, as Houthi forces advance on the southern city of Aden and other strategic areas.
Yemeni government forces said on Sunday they had withdrawn from Dhubab airport and territory they held near the Bab al-Mandeb strait, southwest of Yemen, to defend Aden, the de facto seat of the government.
Retired Lebanese Brigadier-General Hassan Jouni, a military and strategic expert, said fighting is now focused on control over a mountainous triangle of territory in southern Yemen, which could decide the outcome of the war.
This area links Aden to Taiz, another city held by the government but encircled by the Houthis – an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God) – and Bab al-Mandeb, a maritime chokepoint that connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.
“This triangle is the strategic centre of gravity for the war in Yemen as a whole,” Jouni told Al Jazeera.
On Sunday, government-aligned forces were withdrawn from Dhubab, which was recaptured from the Houthis in September, to avoid an imminent siege in the coastal strip by the Houthis and to help defend Aden, analysts say.
Houthi advances in this southwestern region now threaten to completely cut off the government’s coastal supply routes, Jouni said.
The Yemen war began when the Houthis, a Zaidi Shia group close to Iran, captured the capital, Sanaa, in September 2014, forcing the government to flee south to Aden. Saudi Arabia launched an Arab coalition military campaign to aid the government in March 2015, launching thousands of air strikes against Houthi forces.
Following a relatively peaceful few years, fighting re-erupted in July when government forces’ jets bombed Sanaa international airport to prevent a Houthi delegation from landing in the Yemeni capital.
A Houthi offensive in September saw the government lose control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, including the key port city of Mocha . Later Houthi advances also saw Taiz completely besieged by the Houthis.
Yemeni Armed Forces spokesperson Majed al-Nuzaili defended the retreat from Dhubab, saying it was part of a wider tactical manoeuvre.
“[The redeployment] is an extension of the heroic positions of the popular resistance and the southern forces in protecting the temporary capital Aden,” he said on X.
But Jouni believes the situation faced by government forces is grim, with the Houthis reaching Tor al-Baha, just 80km (50 miles) from Aden.
“The Houthi forces have reached this line, meaning that they are indeed in the defensive line area of the city of Aden. We do not say they have approached Aden, but the defence of the city of Aden begins in this area,” he told Al Jazeera.
“The basic combat direction now is in the vicinity of the besieged city of Taiz. On the other hand, of course, the Houthis will focus their attention now on approaching Aden and controlling the first defensive zone.”
Strategic affairs expert Ali al-Dahab gave a less optimistic assessment of the situation than the one presented by the government.
“What happened is a retreat or a withdrawal with the same meaning, and not a redeployment, because the withdrawal left a vast vacuum filled by the Houthis,” al-Dahab stated.
The government’s “Operation Yemen Dawn” has responded to the situation with a dramatic increase in strikes on Houthi positions, including 900 targeting operations within 24 hours.
The Houthis have responded with ballistic missiles and drone attacks towards Mecca, Riyadh, and the Eastern province in Saudi Arabia. They have announced they will continue operations under a principle of “siege for siege, airport for airport, and escalation for escalation”.
Al-Dahab said this strategy is directed at Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government’s key international ally, and not at authorities in Aden.
With their recent gains on the coast along Bab al-Mandeb, which has become increasingly significant to global maritime trade since the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the US-Israel war on Iran, the Houthis have significant geopolitical leverage.
“They now directly and completely control the western Yemeni coastal sector and part of the maritime extension towards Aden,” al-Dahab warned.
“The matter translates the Houthis’ gains in Bab al-Mandeb in large part to the benefit of Iran.”
