Elektrikli motosiklet üreten Stark Future , 150 milyon eurodan fazla yatırım aldı. Şirketin 150 milyon euroyu aşan yatırım turuna Highland Europe liderlik etti. İspanya merkezli Stark Future'un yatırım turunda Morgan Stanley Investment Management’ın 1GT fonu ve Axon Partners Group yer aldı.
2020 yılında kurulan şirketin değerlemesi 1,2 milyar euroya yükseldi. Stark Future, yeni yatırımı daha geniş elektrikli motosiklet kategorilerine açılmak ve bu pazarlarda pazar payını artırmak için kullanacağını açıkladı.
Anton Wass ve Paul Soucy tarafından hayata geçirilen şirket, yüksek performanslı elektrikli motosikletler geliştiriyor. Stark Future özellikle arazi sürüşüne yönelik elektrikli motosiklet modelleriyle öne çıkıyor. Motokros, enduro ve süpermoto kategorilerinde faaliyet gösteren şirket, geleneksel içten yanmalı motorlara alternatif elektrikli modeller üretiyor. Şirketin amiral gemisi ürün ailesi olan Varg serisi, farklı arazi ve sürüş koşullarına yönelik elektrikli motosiklet modellerini kapsıyor.
Stark Future, motosikletlerinin motor, batarya ve diğer temel teknolojilerini kendi bünyesinde geliştiriyor. Şirketin geliştirdiği teknolojilerin fikri mülkiyet haklarına da kendisi sahip. Stark Future, başlangıçta odaklandığı arazi motosikleti pazarının ötesine geçerek daha geniş elektrikli motosiklet kategorilerine açılmayı hedefliyor. Şirket, yüksek performanslı elektrikli motosikletleri sürdürülebilir bir ulaşım alternatifi olarak konumlandırırken performansı ve sürüş deneyimini ön planda tutuyor.

Romelu Lukaku, Belgium’s all-time leading goalscorer, has announced his retirement from international football after 16 years, saying he was “at peace” with his decision.
“These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. It was a nice ride and I enjoyed every single moment,” Belgium’s record goalscorer said on Instagram on Monday.
With 94 goals in 135 games, Lukaku is the fifth-highest scorer in men’s international football history and featured in four World Cups for the Red Devils, helping them reach the quarterfinals of this year’s tournament before losing to eventual winners Spain.
The 33-year-old, who now plays for Turkish club Fenerbahce, made his debut in 2010 as a teenager and was an unused substitute in Sunday’s 4-1 Nations League win over Italy.
“To the Belgium fans, thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.
“I will never forget those moments. I’m at peace with my decision to stop here,” Lukaku said.
The former Chelsea, Manchester United and Inter Milan forward was part of Belgium’s so-called “golden generation”.
Lukaku, alongside Kevin De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, finished third at the 2018 World Cup, a best-ever finish for Belgium in the tournament, but they failed to lift a trophy during the period.
“I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for,” Lukaku said.
“I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team,” he added.
The national team paid homage to Lukaku shortly after his announcement.
“More than a goalscorer, you have been a leader, a strong personality and an inspiration to generations of Belgian football fans,” said a post on Instagram by the Red Devils. “You have written an incredible chapter in the history of the Red Devils.”
A host of fellow Belgian players also paid tribute to Lukaku.
“Legend, my brother,” midfielder Axel Witsel posted on Instagram.
“So many amazing memories,” the Real Madrid goalkeeper added.
Lukaku’s last appearance for his country came in October’s 4-1 loss to France.
“Beyond his exceptional performances on the pitch, he has been a true leader, with a strong personality and an essential role in the dressing room,” Lukaku’s former teammate and now Belgium’s technical director, Simon Mignolet, said in a statement from the Belgian football association.
“We respect his decision and are deeply grateful to him for everything he has brought to our national team,” the former Liverpool goalkeeper added.
Belgium’s first game without Lukaku will be a Nations League last-eight fixture in March.
“We must now turn our attention to the future and prepare for the Nations League quarterfinals … with the ambition of continuing to make progress as a team,” Mignolet said.

Gérard Depardieu appeared at a courthouse in Paris on Monday for his appeal trial that was due to start
French film star Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexual assault , admitting that his behaviour towards women had often been offensive and offering a "deep and sincere" apology.
On the day that the appeal was due to start in a Paris court, the 77-year-old actor's unexpected mea culpa marks a dramatic reversal of his previous denials of sexual impropriety.
"Justice was pronounced. I was found guilty. I understand and bow to this conviction… I have therefore decided to abandon the appeal," he wrote.
It means he is now guilty in law of abusing two women during a film shoot in Paris five years ago, and his 18-month suspended prison term stands.
"Victory is ours, and we welcome it with head held high," said one of the two women, named only as Amélie, who was at the court.
"There is huge relief because the fight is over. The giant of film has fallen," said the other woman in the case, who is known in court by the false name Sarah.
In his statement, Depardieu appeared to have undergone a major shift from his earlier stance of unapologetic intransigence.
"For a long time on film shoots I hid myself behind provocation and smut. I thought that the remarks I made, and certain gestures that I made, were of no consequence.
"I see now that there is a border between impertinence and offence. Never, ever did I intend to hurt the women with whom I came into contact. But I see now that intention has no bearing on the hurt that people feel.
"Cases before the courts are damaging. Everything got out of hand… including my defence. Many people have suffered in this story. I have not the power to go back in time. I have come to understand that I belonged to a world that has disappeared."
The reference to his defence "getting out of hand" follows widespread criticism of the aggressive line taken by Depardieu's lawyer during the original trial in March last year.
Depardieu's lawyers David-Olivier Kaminski (L) and Delphine Meillet (R) were at the courthouse on Monday for the opening day of their client's appeal trial in Paris
His new lawyers, Delphine Meillet and David-Olivier Kaminski, said that with his admission of guilt Depardieu wanted to "move on", adding that "basically, as he turns 78 years old, he is saying to himself that life is more beautiful than 10 days of court hearings".
In the original trial, Depardieu was said to have touched the two women on intimate parts of the body during the making of Les Volets Verts, which is a film about an ageing actor coming to terms with his declining powers.
He himself admitted to using vulgar language but denied being "a metro-train groper". However, he also said he did not consider touching a woman's buttocks to be an act of "sexual aggression".
The trial was the first time the star of films like Green Card and Cyrano de Bergerac appeared in court on sexual assault charges. Several other women have made similar allegations in the media.
A decision on whether an alleged rape case can come to trial is expected this month.

Independent MP Helen Haines has been released from hospital after an alleged attack last month
Australian politician Helen Haines has said she is "full of gratitude" upon being discharged from hospital, four weeks after she was allegedly attacked with a car and left a double amputee.
The independent MP was struck outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north-east of Melbourne, on October 19, an incident which horrified Australia.
Brendan Nugent, 43, has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official. He has yet to enter pleas.
In her first public comments since the attack, Haines, 65, said she had moved into the rehabilitation stage of her recovery.
"This is a really positive moment, and I am full of gratitude for the expert and compassionate care I received at the Alfred and am receiving in this next stage," Haines said.
"I appreciate the thousands of warm wishes and supportive messages from people across Indi, throughout Australia and around the world. They are giving me strength as I focus on this next phase of healing."
She added that she had been "overwhelmed" by the generosity of well wishers who had donated to Save the Children in her honour.
Haines, known for supporting stronger climate action and helping establish a national anti-corruption commission, entered parliament in 2019 as the Member for Indi after working as a nurse and midwife.
Victoria Police has said its investigation, with support from the Australian Federal Police, remains ongoing and a motive is yet to be established.
Nugent's father said he and his wife had been long-time friends of Haines, and Nugent's lawyer has said his client has mental health concerns.
The incident sparked a reckoning in the country more broadly over the tone of public debate.
Though a motive is still unclear, politicians, law enforcement, and experts have said heated public discourse is heightening the threat of political violence in the country.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he had been in regular contact with Haines and her "extraordinary" family.
"All our thoughts and prayers continue to be with Helen for her recovery," he said in a statement.
"We continue to provide support to Helen, her family, community and staff as she undertakes her rehabilitation."

French actor apologises to two women he was convicted of assaulting on a film set in 2021
The French actor Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set, and has for the first time apologised to the victims.
“I was found guilty. I hear it and I accept this conviction,” Depardieu, 77, said in a written statement. “I address my deep and sincere apologies to those who suffered.”
The actor, who has made more than 200 films and TV series, wrote: “For a long time on film sets, I hid behind provocation and ribald humour.”
He said he accepted that remarks and “some of my gestures” were not “without consequences”, particularly because he held a powerful position in the entertainment industry.
Depardieu said he had never intended to hurt the women he encountered but had “come to understand that intention changes nothing about the harm caused”.
He said times had changed and that he belonged “to a world that no longer exists”.
At a trial last year, Depardieu was found guilty of sexually assaulting a 55-year-old set dresser and a 35-year-old assistant director during the shooting of the feature film Les Volets Verts (The Green Shutters) in Paris in September 2021.
His suspended sentence will now stand and his name must be added to France’s sex offender register.
The set dresser, named in the media as Amélie, said outside the Paris appeal court on Monday: “I waited for years for this apology.” She said she would have preferred if Depardieu had attended court to deliver it in person.
The assistant director, named in the media as Sarah, said: “The monster of cinema has fallen.”
Depardieu’s conviction last year was a turning point for the #MeToo movement in France . He became the biggest figure in the French film industry to be convicted of sexual assault after years of criticism of the country’s reluctance to take women’s claims of abuse seriously.
Depardieu had previously denied all allegations of sexual assault. He told last year’s trial that the media had used allegations against him to damage his reputation.
He attacked the #MeToo movement as well as women who had staged protests outside venues during his concert tour at the time of the allegations. “This movement is going to become a terror,” he said.
The trial also set an important legal precedent when the judge ruled that Depardieu’s defence lawyer, Jérémie Assous, had been “excessively harsh” to the two women in court, saying they were not real victims and were liars.
Assous had said the women were working for the cause of “rabid feminism” and called their lawyers hysterical, “abject and stupid” and described them as having an “unbearable voice”.
The judge awarded the complainants compensation for being further victimised by Depardieu’s defence during the trial, ordering Depardieu to pay each woman €1,000 (£835).
The court had heard there was a “system of impunity” around Depardieu, with film industry insiders staying silent to keep cashing in on his name.
Depardieu has appealed against a separate decision requiring him to face trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting the actor Charlotte Arnould at his Paris home in 2018. Appeal judges will rule this month on whether to uphold his appeal or allow the trial to go ahead next year.
In an open letter to Le Figaro in October 2023, Depardieu denied all allegations and said any encounter with Arnould had been consensual. “Never, ever, have I abused a woman,” he wrote.
In December 2023, when Depardieu was under formal investigation for rape and sexual assault in the Arnould case and also facing scrutiny over sexist comments revealed in a TV documentary, the French president defended him, saying “he makes France proud”.
Asked at the time about stripping Depardieu of a state award, Emmanuel Macron said: “You will never see me participate in a manhunt … I hate that type of thing.”

Traffic temporarily restricted on key connection after bridge targeted during overnight drone barrage by Ukraine
Ukraine has hit the Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea with Russia, in a symbolic blow that temporarily paralysed road traffic and left thousands of drivers stranded.
A Ukrainian kamikaze drone crashed into one of the bridge’s arches at 5.38am local time, local channels reported. Earlier drones could be heard buzzing above the structure, as Russian air defence units opened fire.
The extent of the damage was unclear. One report said the arch was listing at a 15-degree angle and “looked tired”.
The Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea , Sergey Aksyonov, confirmed the “enemy” had launched an attack. “As a result, traffic will be restricted, likely until the afternoon,” he wrote on Telegram.
Russian officials said the crossing would remain closed while experts assessed its condition. About 2,000 vehicles were reportedly stuck in traffic jams on both sides.
In a call with reporters, the Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, downplayed the incident. He said: “Minor damage is being assessed. ⁠Traffic across the bridge continues.”
Ukraine says the bridge is a legitimate target for its armed forces, and has made at least two previous attempts to blow it up.
In 2022 a truck laden with explosives damaged part of the road section. A second strike using a “sea baby” drone took place the following year. Russia has subsequently strengthened air defences and installed metal barges and boom barriers.
Overnight Ukraine launched 1,336 drones, in what the Kremlin says was one of the biggest attacks so far this year. About 600 were intercepted on their approach to Moscow, claimed the capital’s mayor, Sergei Sobyanin.
The barrage took place days before a summit in Shenzhen between China’s president, Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Putin. US officials say the talks will not focus on the war in Ukraine, where Russia’s military offensive has largely stalled.
Ukraine says its retaliatory strikes are justified retribution for Russia’s own missile and drone barrages of its cities and energy grid – attacks that have killed hundreds of civilians and regularly knock out power and heating for millions. In recent weeks Russia has repeatedly hit two critical bridges in Kyiv over the Dnipro river.
Diplomatic efforts on ending the almost five-year war have so far gone nowhere. After a fresh round of talks in Abu Dhabi last week, Putin reiterated his hardline territorial demands and said any deployment of foreign troops would be seen in Moscow as a “continuation of war”.
The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , said on Friday the Trump administration had proposed that Kyiv gives Russia the eastern Donbas region – including towns and villages Russia does not control – in exchange for Nato membership or Nato-like guarantees.
Zelenskyy ruled out handing over territory. The details of possible US security guarantees were vague and did not feature American troops on the ground, he said, citing conversations with Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and the real-estate developer Steve Witkoff. The emissaries last week saw Putin in Moscow.

Germany manager Jurgen Klopp says he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he called for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.
Blatter resigned as Fifa boss in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.
Infantino plans to stand for re-election in March but has been under pressure since scrapping his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which included selling off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.
Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for the plan but was told he was not fit to lead world football's governing body unless he released all the documents and answered key questions.
"I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense," said Klopp.
"I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that."
Klopp added: "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job."
Infantino apologises to Fifa Council - but told he is still not fit to lead
Uefa - European football's governing body - has been one of Infantino's fiercest critics and has repeatedly called on him to stand down.
It has prepared criminal legal proceedings against Infantino and lodged a claim in three US courts for all documents related to FFE to be released.
The deadline for candidates to officially confirm they are standing against Infantino in Fifa's presidential election is Wednesday.
Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who is Fifa's head of global development, had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport he has ruled himself out.
Uefa is said to still be hopeful of finding an alternative candidate before Wednesday's deadline.
Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.
Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.
"There are people who truly care about the future of football - people who aren't driven by financial interests," said Klopp.
"If someone like that were to step up - if someone like that were to become president - I think that would be a significant improvement.
"There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it."

PM’s spokesperson calls message, read out by convicted rapist’s wife on their YouTube channel, ‘clearly appalling’
The Ministry of Justice has launched an investigation into whether Russell Brand has broken prison rules after the jailed comedian shared a message claiming he is not guilty of sexual offences just days after his conviction .
Brand’s wife, Laura Brand, read a message from her rapist husband in a video uploaded to their YouTube channel in which he claimed: “I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for.”
It is understood a prisoner will be deemed to have broken the rules if they provide comments to a family member they know will be published.
Any inquiry could also examine whether the current rules need to be updated to stop comments from prisoners being broadcast via profit-making YouTube channels.
Asked about the comments, the prime minister’s official spokesperson said: “This is clearly appalling and is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules. Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances.
“Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments … This is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if the rules have been broken.”
Brand, 51, is serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison term after he was convicted of one count of rape and three sexual assaults at Southwark crown court on 5 November.
In his message, Brand said he had been moved from the category B Wandsworth prison in south-west London to the lower category C HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire – a prison for men convicted of sexual offences.
Reading the message from a notebook, Laura Brand said: “As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.”
His message added: “I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey, little as in small, and hey as in hey, I’m in the biggest sex offenders’ prison in Europe. The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated. And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone.
“I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me, let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us.”
Responding to the video on Monday, the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, told Sky News: “His crimes are heinous and awful. I think it’s revolting, by the way, that he shows no remorse today in his comments. No remorse, no sympathy for the victims. Just disgusting comments.”
According to official guidance, prisoners are expected to make a formal application through their governor if they wish to contact the media.
Prison sources said current rules may have to be updated to stop people from releasing comments on YouTube channels through which a prisoner or their family may profit via sponsorship or advertising. The rules say: “Correspondence which is intended for publication or for use by radio or television or for posting on the internet (or which if sent, would be likely to be published or broadcast) must not contain material which is for publication in return for payment (unless the prisoner is unconvicted).”

Russell Brand (pictured during his trial) delivered a message to followers via his wife Laura
A message by Russell Brand to his followers in which he claimed innocence for his sexual offences was "clearly appalling" and is being urgently investigated, Downing Street has said.
The comedian is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
His wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, in which the convicted rapist claimed: "I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for."
No 10 said it expects action to be taken if Brand is found to have broken prison rules, while Victims' Commissioner for London Andrea Simon said the claims will "certainly retraumatise his victims and other survivors of rape who have to hear it".
In the couple's podcast, released on Sunday, Laura Brand can seen sitting on a sofa and is holding a Bible with a candle burning in front of her.
Relaying the message from her husband, Laura Brand said the comedian - who is currently being held at HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire - called prison staff "strong", "kind" and "dedicated", and asked people to support his "treasured wife and family".
She said she had been speaking to him and he "is OK and is praying".
Brand has positioned himself as a Christian influencer, and has a large following among believers, including in the US.
Asked about the message, the prime minister's official spokesman said: "Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances.
"Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments."
Speaking earlier, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Sky News: "His crimes are heinous and awful. I think it's revolting, by the way, that he shows no remorse today in his comments."
"No remorse, no sympathy for the victims. Just disgusting comments," he added.
Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Victim's Commisioner for London Simon added: "The victims during the sentencing hearing highlighted how his denials and ongoing media fame over two decades had added to their pain and trauma," she said.
"The fact survivors are still having to hear this now is really problematic and very concerning that we can't do more to protect them from it."
While freedom of expression allows convicted sex offenders such as Brand to profess their innocence, Simon said terms of service of media platforms should regulate "the way in which they get their message out".
She added that prison rules should also be reviewed to "bar those convicted of sending messages to be broadcast" unless permission is granted by the prison governor.
Barristers must stop using rape myths in trials, justice secretary says
Brand moved from Wandsworth to category C prison, his wife confirms on podcast
The Russell Brand I saw in court was not the flamboyant character most people will know
Over the weekend, Brand was moved from the category B HMP Wandsworth in south London to the category C HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire, a prison that mostly houses sex offenders and has tailored programmes for them.
Foreign Office minister Stephen Doughty, told LBC he agreed it was not "a good look" that he'd been moved to a lower security prison.
"I think people want to see him facing the appropriate punishment for what are appalling crimes against women and others and I think the whole episode is shocking," he said.
Meanwhile, there have been calls for a change in the law following Brand's conviction so that sexual relationships between 16 and 17-year-olds and adults would be illegal. The government says a discussion is to take place.
Mia Latter, who has alleged she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16, is among those campaigning for ministers to introduce a staggered age of consent.
She was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. Brand denied the allegations at the time. None of the women were complainants in his recent criminal trial.
Latter, who was known under the pseudonym "Alice" in the 2023 investigation, has now waived her right to anonymity.
In an interview with LBC on Monday, Latter said: "We don't want to criminalise anybody under the age of 18 [including] 16, 17-year-olds, 18-year-olds having sex with each other...
"I think healthy relationships are important, and they're important in helping you develop and grow."
But she said there should be an age "threshold" for the partners of 16 and 17 year-olds.
Layla Stone, founder of the campaign group Close the Consent Gap, is urging a change in the law to prevent 16 year-olds from having a sexual relationship with anyone older than 19, and someone aged 17 from having a relationship with anyone older than 20.
She told BBC Breakfast that "predators know exactly what they are doing".
Asked about the issue on BBC Breakfast, the foreign secretary said: "I think the reason why it's right to have this debate is we've seen some of the very, very brave victims of Russell Brand come forward and say 'we think this needs looking at'."
Shadow education secretary Laura Trott said she is glad there is a conversation around staggering the age of consent but warned that it had "been quite complicated to actually implement" in some US states where it is used.
Trott said a suggestion that the age of consent should be raised to 18 is also a "conversation we need to have" but "probably isn't practical".
Anna Edmundson, director of policy & social change at the NSPCC charity, said: "We urgently need a review of what is and isn't working to ensure 16 and 17-year-olds are fully protected in law from this predatory behaviour.
"However, closing these gaps will only be part of the solution. We must question why adults have been able to exploit teenagers in plain sight for so long, and look at what further action is needed to help people recognise the signs of exploitation."
Any change in the law would only affect England and Wales as Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate legislative powers in relation to the age of consent, which is also currently set at 16 in both nations.
The Scottish Government said it had "no current plans" to change the age of consent, following the calls by campaigners, but any proposals would be considered.
The foreign secretary also apologised for having appeared on Russell Brand's online show in 2015, when he was Labour leader.
Miliband told Today if he'd known about the allegations then, he would not have done spoken to him, adding: "I deeply regret doing that interview and all my sympathies are with those victims."

“This is a really positive moment, and I am full of gratitude for the expert and compassionate care I received at the Alfred [hospital] and am receiving in this next stage,” Haines said.
“I appreciate the thousands of warm wishes and supportive messages from people across Indi, throughout Australia and around the world. They are giving me strength as I focus on this next phase of healing.”
The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said his thoughts were with Haines.
“We continue to provide support to Helen, her family, community and staff as she undertakes her rehabilitation,” Albanese said in a statement.
Haines said she was “overwhelmed” by the many Australians who had donated to the Save the Children charity fundraiser.
Her husband, Phil Haines, had made the request to the public on her behalf to donate to the charity in lieu of flowers in the aftermath of the alleged attack.
As of Monday afternoon, more than $1.46m had been raised for the charity through Haines’s fundraising appeal.
“I am overwhelmed by the generosity of Australians in the form of donations to Save the Children and I look forward to working with them in due course on applying these funds to improve the lives of children.”
Haines, the federal member for the Victorian seat of Indi, had been in a critical but stable condition after she was repeatedly struck by a vehicle in Wangaratta on 19 October. Her condition was then downgraded to “serious but stable” on 24 October.
Police will allege the 65-year-old was standing by the boot of her car outside her electoral office when a car did a U-turn and struck her repeatedly.
Tarrawingee man Brendan Nugent, 43, has been charged and the incident continues to be investigated. He is known to her family.
Police charged Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally cause serious injury and the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official.
Police have also charged him with two additional offences – cultivating and possessing cannabis – according to court documents.
The foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, paid tribute to Haines in the Senate on Monday and on behalf of the parliament wished her strength through her challenging rehabilitation.
“It says a great deal about her character that even as she faces these challenges, in her statement she looks ahead to the work she wants to do to improve the lives of children following the donations to Save the Children that Australians made at her request. It is an example of her determination and her generosity that is so admired,” Wong said.
The leader of the opposition in the Senate, Michaelia Cash, added that Haines’s discharge from hospital was warmly welcomed across the parliament.
“She has demonstrated extraordinary courage and resilience. And on behalf, in particular, of my Coalition Senate colleagues, we wish Helen every strength during her continued recovery.”
Haines has been given leave of absence until 26 November, the last sitting day of the year.
MPs across parliament have expressed concern for their safety and that of their staff since the alleged attack, and prompted conversations about the temperature of political debate.
Albanese, during the last parliamentary sitting, warned against the rise in anger “that distorts and corrodes our public discourse”, and urged voters and politicians not to ignore it.
“Enabled by the anonymity and speed afforded by social media, we are seeing rage and aggression increasing, not just in politics, but towards workers in hospitality and retail, in schools and in hospitals, towards police, paramedics, and other officials, we are seeing a normalisation of the language of grievance and violence.”
The independent MP Allegra Spender said it was “wonderful” news that Haines was making good progress in her recovery.
“She is a remarkable person and her strength and positivity after everything that has happened inspires me.”

The Estonian government says it will shut the crossings after accusing Russia of directing an alleged sabotage attack on a drone manufacturer
Estonia has said it will close border crossings into Russia from 1 December after accusing Moscow of being behind an attempted arson attack at a drone factory.
Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the break-in on Saturday at a facility north of the capital Tallinn was part of what he called Russia's "broader hybrid war against Europe".
The alleged attackers were arrested, Michal said, with local media reporting the suspects are Latvian.
They are said to have broken into the factory and attempted to set fire to it using flammable liquids.
On Monday, Moscow said the accusation was "baseless" and accused the Estonian government of "building a wall" between the neighbouring countries.
The facility targeted is operated by Threod Systems and produces attack and reconnaissance drones, with Ukraine and Nato member states listed as customers on its website.
Foreign minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that "closing the border crossings will reduce Russia's ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia".
Michal said "extensive damage was averted thanks to heightened security measures" at the factory, while the head of Estonia's internal security service labelled the incident attempted Russian sabotage.
The decision to close border crossings is expected to be finalised next week, according to local media.
Estonia shares a border of around 220 miles (338 km) with Russia that spans both sea and land. Three road crossings are in operation but are already subject to restrictions.
One of them is located at Narva, Estonia's third biggest city. It sits on the western bank of the River Narva that flows into the Baltic Sea; on the eastern bank is Russia. Closures will complicate life for families which live either side of the border.
Kremlin spokesman Dimitry Peskov said: "Estonia is building a wall. Many countries, as history demonstrates, have built walls that have brought nothing good to those who erect such walls."
Russia has been repeatedly accused by European leaders of targeting national infrastructure and resources destined for Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.
Baltic region leaders have repeatedly accused Russia of hybrid attacks and raised fears about the Kremlin's territorial ambitions.
Other major backers of Ukraine in Europe, including France, Germany, the UK and Poland, have also said Russia has orchestrated attacks on their soil in recent months.
Last year, six men were jailed in the UK over an arson attack linked to Russia at a London warehouse where aid bound for Ukraine was being stored.

Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced an "attempted coup" on Monday following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election.
"As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: This wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup," Yair Lapid, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list, wrote on X.
Israel's Channel 12 television reported on Sunday that on the eve of the 27 October election, Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party.
Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source, a former employee of Netanyahu's office, who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members.
The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded.
Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations.
The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence.
Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an "attempted coup by Netanyahu".
"If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu," he wrote on X.
Raam's number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.
"These suspicions require an immediate, independent and thorough criminal investigation that reaches everyone involved, at every level and in every role," he wrote on X.
"Netanyahu cried out that his election was being stolen, while he himself tried to steal the country and is still trying to do so now," he added.
Netanyahu's main rival, former army chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, wrote on Sunday that the caretaker prime minister "cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer".
Neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Eisenkot's opposition secured the 61 seats required to form a government following last month's election.
The two Arab parties, the Joint List and Raam, have indicated support for Eisenkot who was tasked by President Isaac Herzog with forming a government.

The race is led by a number of female artists, also including Phoebe Bridgers and Ella Langley, with Beyoncé receiving her record-breaking 100th nomination
Raye is leading this year’s female-heavy Grammys race with 11 nominations.
The British singer-songwriter, who has received four nominations in the past, picked up nods in categories including song of the year, songwriter of the year and album of the year.
The other artists nominated for album of the year are Phoebe Bridgers, Olivia Dean, Ella Langley, Bruno Mars, Raye, Olivia Rodrigo, Taylor Swift and Rosalía, who came in second with nine nominations.
The Spanish star received nods in categories including best alternative music performance, best music video and record of the year for Berghain .
The other nominees for record of the year are Tame Impala and Jenny – Dracula, Olivia Dean – Man I Need, Ella Langley – Choosin’ Texas, Bruno Mars – I Just Might, Raye – Where is my Husband?, Taylor Swift – The Fate of Ophelia and Olivia Rodrigo – The Cure.
Rodrigo, who has won three Grammys previously, scored seven nominations putting her in third position with Bridgers, Miranda Lambert and Langley, who broke out this year with record-breaking hit Choosin’ Texas .
Langley leads the category of best new artist alongside Angine De Poitrine , Geese , Slayyyter , Sienna Spiro , Don Toliver, Remi Wolf and The Womack Sisters . Last year’s award was won by Dean , who received six nominations this year.
Beyoncé received her 100th nomination, this year for best R&B solo performance. She remains the most nominated artist of all time at the Grammys. She is also the most awarded with 35 wins.
The most nominated male artists are Leon Thomas and Bruno Mars , with six nods apiece. Mars has previously won 35 awards.
Madonna, who has won seven Grammys in her career, picked up four nominations including best dance/electronic album, and best pop duo/group performance with Sabrina Carpenter. Other artists who received dance/electronic nominations include Slayyyter, Zara Larsson and Tinashe.
Swift received five nominations for both her The Life of a Showgirl album and I Knew It, I Knew You, her Toy Story 5 song.
Despite ongoing controversy over his antisemitic comments, Kanye West (Ye) picked up a nomination for best rap album for Bully – Deluxe. He was nominated alongside Busta Rhymes and J Dilla, Cardi B, Rapsody, Don Toliver and Wale.
Dolly Parton, who died in August, also received three posthumous nominations, including best country duo/group performance. Tim Curry, who also died in August, was also nominated in the audiobook category.
Morgan Freeman, who has previously been nominated for a spoken word album, picked up a nomination for his blues album.
The newly introduced category of best Asian pop music performance has already led to controversy with members of BTS refusing to submit their music as a result. “We hope our music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” a joint statement read.
Other first-time categories include best Latin song, which was led by Karol G and Rosalía; best traditional pop vocal performance, which featured Olivia Dean and Raye; and best R&B collaboration or duo/group performance, which saw nominees including Chris Brown featuring Leon Thomas and Jill Scott featuring JID.
Notable snubs included Harry Styles, Justin Bieber Gracie Abrams, Sam Smith, Luke Combs, Katseye and Ed Sheeran, who all received no nominations. Despite acclaim for her album West End Girl , Lily Allen also received just one nod for the artwork.
Harvey Mason Jr, CEO of the Recording Academy, referenced concerns over artificial intelligence in his introduction, stating that at this time it is “so important that we honour the human creators behind the music”.
Last year’s awards were dominated by wins from Bad Bunny and Kendrick Lamar.
The ceremony is scheduled to take place on 7 February at the Crypto.com arena in Los Angeles. A host has yet to be announced.

The drugs agency described the seized package as a "potent strain of cannabis"
A basketball player from the US has been arrested in Nigeria with 33.95kg (75lbs) of cannabis in his luggage at the main airport in Lagos.
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) identified the player as Greene Da'monte Khiree, 28, from the US state of Georgia, who it said had arrived from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.
According to the agency, the suspect said he had been playing professional basketball in Thailand and was visiting to Nigeria to "build networks" for his career. He has not publicly commented on the allegations.
The agency said an examination of the suspect's phone had pointed "to his knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity".
In statement on Sunday, the agency said he was arrested on Wednesday after airport officials noticed him abandoning his two checked-in bags and attempting to leave with his carry-on bag.
The two bags, which bore his name, contained 32 packs of the drug known as "Loud", a potent strain of cannabis, the agency said.
A tracking device was also recovered from the bags, the agency added.
The International Basketball Federation (FIBA) lists a player by the name Damonte Greene, with the most recent appearance at the Phuket Elite Cup in Thailand, on 26 September.
Greene played with the Reinhardt University's basketball team in the US in the 2017-2018 season, before he went to play at the South Georgia Technical College.
He was the leading scorer with Georgia Bombers semi-professional basketball team during the 2023-24 season before he moved to Thailand.
Nigeria, once regarded primarily as a transit hub for drug trafficking, has increasingly become a producer, consumer, and distributor of illegal drugs, according to the UN.
Recent NDLEA operations have uncovered several industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratories, raising concerns about links between Nigerian drug producers and Mexican cartels seeking to manufacture and export the drug.
In September, the agency said it had dismantled a meth lab and arrested a Mexican suspected drug kingpin who was allegedly attempting to flee Nigeria through Lagos.
Methamphetamine, commonly known as meth, is a highly addictive synthetic drug that can cause severe psychosis, heart attacks or stroke.
In August, a social media influencer suspected of links to an international drug trafficking network was arrested after the authorities seized cocaine worth nearly $28m (£21m), which was destined for the UK.

double quotation mark This is clearly appalling and is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules.

Nearly 2,200 migrants arrived by boat in Spain’s Canary Islands over two days, according to the country’s maritime rescue service.
On Sunday, November 15, rescue teams assisted migrants aboard crowded boats off the island of El Hierro, helping passengers, including a baby, disembark safely at port facilities.
The Maritime Rescue Service said it had assisted 1,324 people aboard 14 boats, most of whom arrived on El Hierro. The figure was close to the daily record for the Atlantic migration route, set in November 2020.
The Canary Islands remain a major entry point for migrants attempting the dangerous Atlantic crossing from West Africa to Spain. More than 13,000 people reached the archipelago by sea between January and the end of October, according to Spain’s Interior Ministry.

Authorities say measure is part of ongoing efforts to reduce cybercrime and strengthen digital security.
Jordanian authorities have banned the Telegram messaging app, saying the move aims to curb the dissemination of illegal content and what they describe as “extremist material”.
The Public Security Directorate (PSD) announced the measure in a statement published on Monday amid a security crackdown after nine people were killed in an attack on a Greek Orthodox church last month.
The PSD urged citizens to “exercise caution when using social media applications, to avoid interacting with accounts, links, or entities of unknown origin, and to report any unlawful practices or content through official channels”.
The church shooting took place in the village of Hammoud in the west-central governorate of Karak. On Sunday, three men were sentenced to death by hanging over the attack.
The incident prompted Jordan to carry out air strikes on neighbouring Syria that Amman said killed 20 members of the ISIL (ISIS) armed group linked to the church attack.
Meanwhile, a security officer was killed and another wounded this month in Amman in what authorities described as another “terrorist attack”.
Telegram, founded by Russian entrepreneur Pavel Durov in 2013, is believed to be used by groups such as ISIL. In July, Russia issued an arrest warrant for Durov, accusing him of aiding “terrorism”.
The 42-year-old is currently believed to be in Dubai in the United Arab Emirates and faces up to life in a Russian prison if found guilty. He is also being investigated in several other countries.
Telegram supports end-to-end encrypted chats, but not all conversations are encrypted. The messaging app is popular in the Middle East and North Africa. The region accounts for about 8 percent of global users.

An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.
Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player it named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.
The NDLEA said the player told them he had come to Nigeria to “build networks” for his basketball career. The agency said evidence on his phone suggested he had “knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity”. The NDLEA said it detained the player when he attempted to leave the airport with his hand luggage after abandoning two checked-in bags. The agency said those two bags were found to contain 32 parcels of marijuana, and a tracking device.
Nigeria has strict drug laws, and trafficking carries a sentence of life in prison.
A basketball player by the name of Damonte Greene is listed on the roster of the Pattani Raptors in the Thai Premier Men’s League. Greene, a Georgia native, played college basketball for Reinhardt University and South Georgia Technical College. He played semi-professional basketball in the US before representing a number of teams in Thailand.
WNBA star Brittney Griner and former Utah State player Jarred Shaw were imprisoned in Russia and Indonesia respectively for marijuana offenses. Griner was released in December 2022, while Shaw remains in prison .

Pontiff delivers forceful speech in Peru as he travels from high in the Andes into the Amazon
Pope Leo XIV has demanded justice for environmental defenders killed for protecting the Amazon and backed efforts by Indigenous peoples to stop their lands from being ravaged by logging and illegal mining.
On the penultimate day of his South American tour, Leo on Sunday travelled into the Peruvian Amazon and channelled one of Pope Francis’s core teachings that links care for the most vulnerable with care for God’s creation.
“The cry of the Earth and the cry of the poor are inseparable,” Leo told Indigenous representatives and missionaries gathered along the Ucayali River in the north-eastern city of Pucallpa.
He said he came to Pucallpa to support them in their search for justice and peace and referred to what environmental groups estimate have been 57 murders of environmental defenders between 2010 and 2024.
“The blood of these brothers cries out to God and demands justice,” Leo said to applause from the crowd, many of whom were wearing traditional feathered headwear and face markings of the region.
In addition to deforestation, illegal gold mining has become an increasingly lucrative business in the Amazon, devastating forests and polluting rivers. Illegal mining and coca production has also driven deforestation .
Leo addressed the combination of threats in one of his most forceful speeches to date, drawing on his years of experience as a Peruvian bishop and Francis’s constant preaching about the environment and the plight of Indigenous groups.
During the encounter and a subsequent mass in Pucallpa, he demanded a different model of economic development that respects the Earth and the Indigenous peoples who care for it, rather than the “irresponsible exploitation” by outside actors.
“Very little has been done – and very slowly at that – while the means to exploit and pollute creation have accelerated,” he said at mass. “In the face of these evils, let us not bury the Lord’s gifts, for he gives us the strength to repair and heal the suffering caused by an insatiable thirst for domination.”
In Peru, most murders of environmental defenders go unpunished; only a few have resulted in convictions.
The most recent conviction came in the case of Kichwa leader Quinto Inuma Alvarado, who was murdered in 2023 when he was ambushed by hitmen on a river in the San Martín region, the Amazonian territory he was defending.
Leo also referred to a notorious rise in sexual violence against Indigenous Awajún and Wampis schoolgirls in the northern Amazon, and blasted the “impunity” and “corruption” surrounding them.
The Awajún and Wampis Women’s Council has recorded 370 cases of sexual violence in the Condorcanqui province between January and July.
Julio Cusurichi, an Indigenous leader, handed Leo a letter during his visit to Pucallpa, asking him to help protect the rights of uncontacted Indigenous relatives.
“The Peruvian state is weakening the mechanisms that should safeguard their territories,” said the letter from the Indigenous rights organisation Aidesep, on which Cusurichi is a board member.
“We cannot allow economic interests to take precedence over the lives and rights of these vulnerable peoples. Therefore, we ask Pope Leo XIV to raise his voice and support this urgent call for their defence.”
Cardinal Pedro Barreto praised the pope’s decision to meet with Indigenous peoples. Barreto, a former Peruvian archbishop who helped win a multimillion-dollar pollution payout for an Andean town, said: “[Leo] is well aware of all the historical suffering … corruption, illegal mining, deforestation, and the contempt shown by politicians.”
Luis E Fernandez, co-founder of Cincia, a scientific research centre in Peru, also hailed the pontiff’s power to raise awareness. “Pope Leo’s recognition of pollution from illegal mining brings much-needed attention to a crisis affecting Indigenous and riverine communities across the Amazon,” he said.
Fernandez visited the Vatican in October and presented Leo with scientific evidence detailing the impact of illegal gold mining and associated mercury poisoning.
Leo’s last full day in Peru was also his most ambitious, crisscrossing the nation to minister to communities high in the Andes mountains. Peru’s air force released footage of the pope inside a helicopter and said it was “an unforgettable memory” to take Leo around the country.
His first stop was the mountain city of Cusco, where huge crowds greeted him.
“It is all worth it,” said Margarida Salomon, 63, who said she came from Sucre in Bolivia to see the pontiff, spending about $500 to take a bus and sleep in a tent. “I am still getting to know this pope, but the fact he is here in the Andes means a lot.”
The visit to Cusco, 3,400m (more than 11,000ft) above sea level, tested Leo’s stamina as he continues recovering from lung cancer surgery last month. Leo sat in the chair of his popemobile during part of the ride around Cusco, but it wasn’t clear if that was to preserve his energy or to steady himself on the uneven streets.
In general, the 71-year-old Leo has seemed unfazed by the toll of the three-nation South American trip , the longest of his pontificate.

Nihayet "You Can See Everything"i izleyebileceğimiz hafta geldi.
Elbette sözünü ettiğimiz yapım, Nathan Fielder ve Lance Oppenheim'in, hüküm giymiş Amerikalı dolandırıcı Elizabeth Holmes'u konu alan ve şimdiden büyük merak uyandıran belgeseli.
Fragmanının yayımlanması bile internette binlerce internet şakasına ilham verdi. Avrupa'daki bazı gösterim tarihlerinin ertelenmesi ise spoiler'lardan kaçınmayı neredeyse imkânsız hale getirdi. Letterboxd'un o kendine özgü dünyasında dolaşan yorumlar, beklenmedik gelişmelerle dolu üç saatlik bir film izleyicileri beklediğine işaret ediyor.
Film, İngiltere ve İrlanda'da 20 Kasım'da gösterime giriyor. Fransa ve Avrupa'nın diğer bölgelerindeki izleyiciler ise ne yazık ki aralık ayının sonuna kadar beklemek zorunda.
Önümüzdeki günlerin bir diğer dikkat çekici kültür sanat etkinliği ise Paris'teki Musee de l'Homme'da açılacak, zihin değiştirici maddelere odaklanan sergi. Çeşitli maddelerin kökenlerini, etkilerini ve tarihsel bağlamlarını ele alan sergi, bunların kültür ve toplumdaki yerini damgalayıcı yaklaşımlardan uzak bir bakışla yeniden değerlendirmeyi amaçlıyor.
The Wallace Collection'ın yeni sergisi, Toskana'nın ilk büyük dükü Cosimo I de' Medici'nin dünyasını beş önemli tarihî eser üzerinden keşfe çıkarıyor.
Floransa'daki Palazzo Pitti'yi genişletmesinden, Agnolo Bronzino gibi dönemin önde gelen Maniyerist ressamlarına eserler sipariş etmesine kadar Cosimo I, sanatı ve zanaatkârlığı siyasi gücünü pekiştirmek için kullandı. Bu yaklaşımıyla İtalyan kültür tarihinin öne çıkan figürlerinden biri haline geldi.
Sergide yer alan eserler, sanatın ve ihtişamın iktidarla kurduğu ilişkiyi gözler önüne seriyor. Bunlar arasında 1574 tarihli, 70 santimetre uzunluğunda bir maiolika şarap soğutucusu ile aslan başı biçiminde kabzaya sahip törensel bir kısa kılıç da bulunuyor.
Uyuşturucu kavramı, zamanla tabu ve damgalamayla özdeşleşti. Bu maddeleri eğlence amacıyla kullananlara ilişkin önyargılar da çoğu zaman tartışmanın önüne geçti. Oysa psikoaktif maddelerin ardındaki tarih ve toplumsal gerçeklik çok daha karmaşık. Paris'teki Musée de l'Homme'da açılan yeni sergi, tam da bu karmaşık tabloyu gözler önüne seriyor.
Günlük hayatta tükettiğimiz kafeinden tarihî afyon şişelerine ve bitki örneklerine uzanan geniş bir seçki sunan sergi, psikoaktif maddelerin tarih boyunca toplum üzerindeki sosyolojik, psikolojik ve ekonomik etkilerini inceliyor. Yerleşik yargıları sorgulamaya davet eden sergi, ziyaretçilere bu maddelerin tarihine ve kültürel bağlamına farklı bir perspektiften bakma fırsatı sunuyor.
Ekstra öne çıkan: Kasım saat 20.00'de Theatre Antoine Riboud'da düzenlenecek program, Lumiere Kardeşler tarafından icat edilen sinematografın tarihini ve sinema sanatının başlangıcını kutlayacak.
Eylül ayında Telluride Film Festivali'nde prömiyer yapan ve nihayet Avrupa genelinde gösterime giren "You Can See Everything" kadar ses getiren çok az belgesel oldu. Nihayet! Çünkü filmle ilgili spoiler'lardan kaçınmak hiç de kolay değildi.
Lance Oppenheim ("Primetime") ve komedi dünyasının sıra dışı isimlerinden Nathan Fielder'ın ("The Curse", "The Rehearsal") imzasını taşıyan film, Elizabeth Holmes'un dünyasına yaklaşık üç saatlik bir yolculuk sunuyor. Belgesel, Holmes'un yatırımcıları kan testi girişimi Theranos aracılığıyla dolandırmaktan aldığı hapis cezasından önceki haftalarda çekilen görüntülere dayanıyor. Ancak film, bir dolandırıcılık hikâyesi anlatmanın çok ötesine geçiyor. Algı, performans, medya ve hakikat kavramlarını psikolojik gerilim ve kara mizahla harmanlayan yapım, izleyicinin beklentilerini ustalıkla ters yüz ediyor.
Bir diğer öne çıkan yapım: Mahershala Ali, "Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother" filminde ailesini korumak için harekete geçen dindar bir tetikçiyi canlandırıyor. Filmin İngiltere'deki gösterim tarihi 20 Kasım.
1996'daki bir uçak kazasından sağ kurtulan bir lise kız futbol takımını konu alan Emmy adayı gerilim dizisi, dördüncü ve son sezonuyla geri dönüyor. Geçmiş ile bugün arasında gidip gelen anlatı, Juliette Lewis, Melanie Lynskey ve Christina Ricci'nin de aralarında bulunduğu yıldız oyuncu kadrosuyla, yaklaşan bölümlerde gençlerin kurtarılışını ve topluma zor geri dönüşünü tamamlayacak. Bu arada ortak travmalarının dehşet verici etkisi, 25 yıl sonra bile çatışmayı körüklemeye devam ederken eski bir aşkın geri dönüşü paranoyayı daha da tırmandırıyor. Yeni oyuncular arasında Molly Ringwald ve Eric Stoltz da var.
Ekstra öne çıkan: Kripto para borsası FTX'in yükselişini ve çöküşünü anlatan yeni Netflix biyografik dramı The Altruists, 19 Kasım'da prömiyer yapıyor.
Kalıcı olarak geri döndüklerini söylemek için henüz erken ama Take That şimdilik yeniden sahnede! İngiliz erkek grubu, bu hafta 10. stüdyo albümü "Dreamers"ı yayımlıyor.
Grubun orijinal beş üyesinden Gary Barlow, Mark Owen ve Howard Donald'ın birlikte kaydettiği albüm, Take That'in akılda kalıcı ve enerjik pop sound'una dönüşünü temsil ediyor. Aşk ve umut temalarını işleyen "Dreamers", yıl sonu hüznüne ve tükenmişlik hissine karşı adeta bir panzehir niteliğinde. Pozitif mesajları ve iyimser melodileriyle albüm, tam anlamıyla "yaşa, gül, sev" ruhunu yansıtıyor.
Ekstra öne çıkan: Eşsiz çeşitlilikte ve sinematik retro bir sound için, üçüncü albümü 'Los Bitchos & Friends Vol 1' şu anda yayımlanmış olan Londra merkezli grup Los Bitchos'dan başkasına bakmanıza gerek yok.

Pope Leo XIV on Sunday demanded justice for environmental defenders killed while protecting the Amazon and backed Indigenous communities fighting to stop their lands from being ravaged by logging, illegal mining and what he called an “insatiable thirst for domination”.
On the penultimate day of his South American tour, Leo travelled into the Peruvian rainforest and echoed a central teaching of Pope Francis: that care for the most vulnerable and care for creation cannot be separated.
“The cry of the earth and the cry of the poor are inseparable,” he told Indigenous representatives and missionaries gathered on the Ucayali River in Pucallpa, in Peru’s northeast.
He said he had come to support them in their search for justice and peace and referred to the 57 murders of environmental defenders that campaign groups estimate took place between 2010 and 2024.
The visit to Cusco, 3,400 metres (more than 11,000 feet) above sea level, tested Leo’s stamina as he continues his recovering from lung cancer surgery last month.
Drawing on his years as a bishop in Peru and on Francis’ constant preaching on the environment and Indigenous peoples, Leo used the encounter and a Mass that followed to call for an economic model that respects the Earth and those who protect it, rather than the “irresponsible exploitation” practised by outsiders.
“Very little has been done — and very slowly at that — while the means to exploit and pollute creation have accelerated,” he said at Mass. “In the face of these evils, let us not bury the Lord’s gifts, for he gives us the strength to repair and heal the suffering caused by an insatiable thirst for domination.”
Illegal mining and coca production are also driving deforestation and encroaching on Indigenous territories, putting ancestral lands at risk and exposing communities to violence and organised crime.
On Saturday, Peruvian police reported three operations against illegal mining in Madre de Dios, one of the country’s most biodiverse regions, destroying equipment, rafts and engines valued at €3.8 million ($4.1 million).
In Peru, most killings of environmental defenders go unpunished, and convictions are rare. In 2025, the courts upheld 28-year prison sentences for four timber merchants over the murder of four Indigenous people who opposed logging, after a trial lasting a decade.
The most recent conviction came in the case of Kichwa leader Quinto Inuma Alvarado, ambushed and killed by hitmen on a river in the San Martín region in 2023.
In August, a court sentenced four people to up to 35 years in prison. It found Inuma had filed a complaint against the defendants to stop deforestation and other crimes, including drug trafficking, and that they plotted his death because he had spoken out.
Leo also addressed a sharp rise in sexual violence against Awajún and Wampis schoolgirls in Condorcanqui province, in the northern Amazon, and condemned the “complicity”, “impunity” and “corruption” surrounding it.
The Awajún and Wampis Women’s Council, Comuawuy, has recorded 370 cases of sexual violence in the province between January and July alone.
After persistent demands from women’s groups, specialised prosecutors’ offices were created and the government launched a prevention plan. In January, the Ministry of Women and Vulnerable Populations announced a 32-year prison sentence for a man accused of sexually abusing a 14-year-old girl.
In Peru, most murders of environmental defenders go unpunished; only a few have resulted in convictions.
In 2025, the Peruvian courts upheld a 28-year prison sentence for four timber merchants for the murder of four Indigenous people who opposed logging, following a trial that lasted a decade.
The most recent conviction came in the case of Kichwa leader Quinto Inuma Alvarado, who was murdered in 2023 when he was ambushed by hitmen on a river in the San Martín region, the Amazonian territory he was defending.
Overall, the 71-year-old has appeared unfazed by the three-nation trip, the longest of his pontificate, which began on 6 November.
While others aboard the papal plane have fallen ill, Leo has shown no sign of fatigue and has seemed energised, particularly by the days spent seeing old friends in his former diocese of Chiclayo.
The Pope mostly sat in the chair of his popemobile during part of the ride around Cusco, but it wasn’t clear if that was to preserve his energy or to steady himself on the uneven streets.

Crowds lined the streets of Lima, Peru, on Sunday, 15 November, as the revered Lord of Miracles icon was carried by truck to Las Palmas Air Base, where Pope Leo XIV was due to celebrate Mass the following day. Worshippers waved papal flags and held portraits of the pontiff as the procession made its way through the capital.
One woman scattered flower petals as the icon passed. One of Peru's most cherished religious symbols, the Lord of Miracles was set to be present at the largest gathering of the Pope's visit to the country, on the final day of his 12-day Latin American tour.
Outside the air base, hundreds of Catholics had already begun queuing, prepared to spend the night waiting for a chance to get close to the Pope. Some sang and prayed, while others shared food they had brought with them. Street vendors sold rosaries, T-shirts, portraits and even plush toys depicting Leo XIV.
Some devotees described the overnight wait as a sacrifice worth making, while others expressed hopes that his visit would bring peace and unity. Meanwhile, volunteers entered the air base to prepare for Monday's Mass.

Bakan Ersoy, Türk dünyasının sanat üniversiteleri temsilcileriyle bir araya geldi.
Kültür ve Turizm Bakanı Mehmet Nuri Ersoy , Ankara'da düzenlenen Türk Dünyası Sanat Üniversiteleri Birliği 6. Dönem Toplantısı'na katıldı.
Türk dünyasının ortak kültürel ve sanatsal mirasının korunması ve uluslararası alanda tanıtılmasına yönelik çalışmalara dikkat çeken Ersoy, Uluslararası Türk Dünyası Müzik Festivali'nin hayata geçirilmesine ilişkin gelişmeler ile Avrupa ve ABD'de düzenlenmesi planlanan konser, panel ve konferansların toplantının gündeminde olduğunu belirtti.
Bakan Ersoy, ekonomik ve savunma alanındaki iş birlikleri kadar kültürel bağların güçlendirilmesinin de büyük önem taşıdığını vurguladı.
BAKAN ERSOY: KÜLTÜREL BAĞLARIMIZI DİRİ TUTMAK EN ÖNEMLİ BAŞLIĞIMIZDIR
Kültür ve Turizm Bakanı Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, Ankara Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Üniversitesinin ev sahipliğinde gerçekleştirilen Türk Dünyası Sanat Üniversiteleri Birliği 6. Dönem Toplantısı'na katıldı.
Türk dünyasının farklı ülkelerinden üniversite rektörleri, akademisyenler ve kültür temsilcilerini bir araya getiren toplantının gündeminde, sanat üniversiteleri arasındaki iş birlikleri, ortak kültürel projeler ve uluslararası etkinliklere yönelik çalışmalar yer aldı.
Toplantıda konuşan Bakan Ersoy, Türk dünyasının ortak medeniyet birikimine dikkat çekerek kültürel ve sanatsal iş birliklerinin ülkeler arasındaki bağları güçlendiren temel unsurlardan biri olduğunu ifade etti.
Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın ekim ayında 13. Türk Devletleri Teşkilatı Zirvesi'ne ev sahipliği yaptığını hatırlatan Bakan Ersoy, geçtiğimiz hafta gerçekleştirilen 6. Korkut Ata Film Festivali'nin ardından Türk dünyasının sanat üniversitelerinin temsilcilerini Ankara'da ağırlamaktan duyduğu memnuniyeti dile getirdi.
Türk dünyasının ortak tarih, kültür ve medeniyet değerleri etrafında buluştuğunu belirten Ersoy, toplantının geleceğe yönelik iş birliklerinin geliştirilmesi açısından önemli bir fırsat sunduğunu söyledi.
Bakan Ersoy, “Bugün burada asırlardır aynı medeniyetin izlerini taşıyan, ortak kültürü paylaşan, birbirinin başarısıyla mutlu olan ve üzüntüsüyle dertlenen Türk dünyasının sanat üniversiteleri akademisyenleri bir araya geldi.” ifadelerini kullandı.
Toplantının gündeminde Türk dünyasının ortak kültürel ve sanatsal mirasını uluslararası alanda tanıtacak projelerin bulunduğunu belirten Ersoy, özellikle müzik alanındaki iş birliklerine dikkat çekti.
Birlik bünyesindeki üniversitelerin geleceğe yönelik faaliyetlerinin, ortak projelerinin ve iş birliği imkânlarının ele alınacağını belirten Ersoy, Uluslararası Türk Dünyası Müzik Festivali'nin hayata geçirilmesine ilişkin gelişmelerin de değerlendirileceğini bildirdi.
Avrupa ve ABD'de düzenlenmesi planlanan konser, panel ve konferansların da gündemde olduğunu ifade eden Bakan Ersoy, şöyle konuştu:
“Bu adımlar neticesinde Türk dünyasının zengin müzik birikimini uluslararası platformlarda daha görünür hale getireceğiz. Türk Dünyası Sanat Üniversiteleri Birliği, ortak medeniyetimizin çağdaş dünyadaki kültürel ve sanatsal temsil gücünü artıracak önemli bir fırsattır.”
Dünyada yaşanan küresel gelişmelerin Türk dünyası ülkelerinin ortak değerler etrafında kenetlenmesinin ve birlikte hareket etmesinin önemini bir kez daha ortaya koyduğunu vurgulayan Bakan Ersoy, gelecek nesillere güçlü ve birlik içinde bir Türk dünyası bırakılması gerektiğini ifade etti.
Ülkeler arasında ekonomik iş birliği, savunma alanında koordinasyon ve uluslararası kuruluşlarda uyumun önemine işaret eden Ersoy, kültürel bağların korunmasının da öncelikli konular arasında yer aldığını belirtti.
Bakan Ersoy, “Bugünün devlet adamlarının çocuklarımıza güçlü ve birlikte bir Türk dünyası bırakma yolunda önemli bir sorumluluğu bulunmaktadır. Jordan on Monday announced a ban on instant messaging service Telegram after a deadly attack on a church last month.
Jordan's ‌Public ⁠Security Directorate said the move aimed to protect the society from "the attempts to spread extremism and radicalisation."
All of which pose a "threat to societal security and national interests," it said.
In December 2022, Jordan also banned TikTok over videos authorities claimed "promoted killing and chaos."
The ban on Telegram comes after a shooting on October 23 at a Greek Orthodox church in the southern Karak governate which left seven people dead and another 34 wounded.
Jordan, in retaliation, organised airstrikes on neighbouring Syria and said it had killed 20 so-called "Islamic State" militants. The government also acknowledged that a number of civilians had been killed in the strikes.
A Jordanian court sentenced three men to death by hanging on Sunday in connection with the attack. Authorities identified them as "followers of a hardline Islamist ideology."
Attacks on Christian minorities are very rare in Jordan, a relatively stable Middle Eastern state and close ally of the United States and which maintains diplomatic and military relations with neighboring Israel.
Christians make up around 3% of Jordan's population of 10 million. The Levantine country is home to one of the oldest Christian communities in the world.
The media and communications authority in Iraq said on Monday the ban was to pressure Telegram to review Iraqi content and "take measures to prevent violations."
"The operating company ​failed to take the necessary measures to address non-compliant content published on the platform and did not adhere to Iraqi laws," the authority said in a statement.
It gave Telegram 30 days ⁠to ​comply, with no indication of what action would follow.
Over the years, so-called "Islamic State" militants have used Telegram for propaganda and communication purposes.
The Russian-born billionaire Pavel Durov, now based in Dubai, built the Telegram messaging app with his brother Nikolai and launched it in 2013.

Şarkıcı İrem Derici, Kıbrıs konseri öncesinde nişanlısı Melih Kunukçu ile ne zaman evleneceği sorusuna “Paramız kalmadı!” yanıtını verdi. Daha önce aralık ayında evlenmeyi planladıklarını söyleyen Derici, yaz boyunca kazandığı parayı evinin tadilatına harcadığını anlattı. Nikahın ertelendiğine dair kesin bir açıklama ise yapmadı.
Şarkıcı İrem Derici'ye Kıbrıs konseri öncesinde en çok sorulan soru, nişanlısı Melih Kunukçu ile ne zaman dünyaevine gireceği oldu. Ancak Derici'nin verdiği yanıt, düğün tarihini bekleyenlerin tahmin ettiği türden değildi.
Kıbrıs'taki konserinden önce basın mensuplarının sorularını yanıtlayan İrem Derici, evlilik sorusu gelince lafı dolandırmadı. Ünlü şarkıcı, kısa ve net bir cümleyle 'Paramız kalmadı!' dedi.
Derici, daha önce Melih Kunukçu ile aralık ayında evlenmeyi planladıklarını söylemişti. Peki para nereye gitti? Şarkıcının anlattığına göre yaz boyunca konserlerden kazandığı tüm birikim, evinin tadilatına harcandı.
Durumunu kendine has esprili diliyle özetleyen Derici, 'Ben bütün yaz eve çalıştım. Kasa boş, kasa bomboş!' ifadelerini kullandı.
Ancak şarkıcının sözlerinde nikahın ertelendiğine dair kesin bir açıklama yer almadı. Çiftin aralık planını koruyup korumadığı ise şimdilik belirsiz. Derici'nin bu dobra çıkışı, şarkıcının daha önce de pek çok konuda sözünü sakınmayan tavrını hatırlattı.
İrem Derici ve DJ-prodüktör Melih Kunukçu, 2026 yılının başında Avustralya 'nın Sidney kentinde nişanlanmıştı. Çiftin başlangıçta 2027 yılında evlenmeyi düşündüğü biliniyordu.
Ağustos ayının sonunda ise Kunukçu'nun adı, Gaziantep merkezli yasa dışı bahis soruşturmasına karıştı. Tutuklanan Kunukçu, Gaziantep 6. Sulh Ceza Hakimliği'nin kararıyla 10 Eylül'de tahliye edildi. Hukuki süreç ise henüz sona ermedi.
O zorlu günlerde nişanlısının yanında olduğunu açıkça gösteren Derici, cezaevindeki Kunukçu'nun doğum günü için yaptığı paylaşımda 'Yolumuza ne tümsekler çıktı ama biz her şeyin üstesinden geldik. O yüzüğü boşuna takmadık. Sonsuza dek yanındayım' demişti.
Nişanlısının eve dönmesiyle sevincini paylaşan Derici, o günlerde magazin basınına 'Artık bizimle alakalı sadece düğün haberi paylaşacağınız günlere inşallah' diye seslenmişti. Tahliyenin ardından konuşan Kunukçu da düğünü 2026'ya çekebileceklerinin sinyalini vermişti.

Sanayi ve Teknoloji Bakanı Mehmet Fatih Kacır, Antalya’da COP31 kapsamında “Yapay Zeka Destekli Temiz Teknolojiler Girişimi Tanıtım Programı”nda konuşuyor.
AK Parti Sözcüsü Ömer Çelik, partisinin MYK gündemine ilişkin açıklamalarda bulunuyor.
Bakanlıktan yapılan açıklamaya göre, Ersoy, Ankara Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Üniversitesinin ev sahipliğinde gerçekleştirilen Türk Dünyası Sanat Üniversiteleri Birliği 6. Dönem Toplantısı'na katıldı.
Ersoy, toplantıda yaptığı konuşmada, Türk dünyasının ortak medeniyet birikimine dikkati çekerek, kültürel ve sanatsal işbirliklerinin ülkeler arasındaki bağları güçlendiren temel unsurlardan biri olduğunu vurguladı.
Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın, ekim ayında 13. Türk Devletleri Teşkilatı Zirvesi'ne ev sahipliği yaptığını anımsatan Ersoy, kısa süre önce gerçekleştirilen 6. Korkut Ata Film Festivali'nin ardından Türk dünyasındaki sanat üniversitelerinin temsilcilerini Ankara'da ağırlamaktan duyduğu memnuniyeti ifade etti.
Türk dünyasının ortak tarih, kültür ve medeniyet değerleri etrafında buluştuğunu dile getiren Ersoy, toplantının geleceğe yönelik işbirliklerinin geliştirilmesi açısından önemli bir fırsat sunduğuna dikkati çekti.
Toplantının gündeminde Türk dünyasının ortak kültürel ve sanatsal mirasını uluslararası alanda tanıtacak projelerin bulunduğunu belirten Ersoy, özellikle müzik alanındaki işbirliklerine dikkati çekti.
Bakan Ersoy, birlik bünyesindeki üniversitelerin geleceğe yönelik faaliyetlerinin, ortak projelerinin ve işbirliği imkanlarının ele alınacağı toplantıda Uluslararası Türk Dünyası Müzik Festivali'nin hayata geçirilmesine ilişkin gelişmelerin de değerlendirileceğini bildirdi.
Avrupa ve ABD'de düzenlenmesi planlanan konser, panel ve konferansların da gündemde olduğunu kaydeden Ersoy, "Bu adımlar neticesinde Türk dünyasının zengin müzik birikimini uluslararası platformlarda daha görünür hale getireceğiz. Türk Dünyası Sanat Üniversiteleri Birliği, ortak medeniyetimizin çağdaş dünyadaki kültürel ve sanatsal temsil gücünü artıracak önemli bir fırsattır." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
Dünyada yaşanan küresel gelişmelerin, Türk dünyası ülkelerinin ortak değerler etrafında kenetlenmesinin ve birlikte hareket etmesinin önemini bir kez daha ortaya koyduğunu anlatan Ersoy, gelecek nesillere güçlü ve birlik içinde bir Türk dünyası bırakılması gerektiğini ifade etti.
Ülkeler arasında ekonomik işbirliği, savunma alanında koordinasyon ve uluslararası kuruluşlarda uyumun önemine işaret eden Ersoy, kültürel bağların korunmasının da öncelikli konular arasında yer aldığını söyledi.
"Bugünün devlet adamlarının çocuklarımıza güçlü ve birlikte bir Türk dünyası bırakma yolunda önemli bir sorumluluğu bulunmaktadır. Ülkelerimiz arasında ekonomik olarak iş birliği, savunma alanında güçlü koordinasyon, uluslararası kuruluşlarda tam uyum önemlidir. Ancak kültürel olarak bağlarımızı diri tutmak da en önemli başlığımızdır."
Sanat üniversitelerinin, ortak kültürel hafızanın korunmasında ve gelecek nesillere aktarılmasında önemli bir sorumluluk üstlendiğini vurgulayan Ersoy, milletlerin köklü geçmişleriyle kurdukları bağın geleceklerini şekillendirdiğini dile getirdi.
Sanat üniversitelerinin kültürel hafızaya sahip çıktığının altını çizen Ersoy, "Milletlerin güçlü köklere sahip olması geleceğe daha umutla bakmasına katkı sağlamaktadır. Kökleri olmayan milletler savrulup gitme tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya kalmaktadır." ifadesini kullandı.
Toplantıda ortaya konulacak ortak iradenin sanat dünyasında kalıcı izler bırakacağına inandığını aktaran Ersoy, organizasyona katkı sunan kurumlara, akademisyenlere ve katılımcılara teşekkür etti.
Program kapsamında Ankara Müzik ve Güzel Sanatlar Üniversitesi Rektörü Prof. Dr. Gülçin Yahya Kaçar tarafından bir sunum gerçekleştirildi.
Türk dünyasının farklı ülkelerinden üniversite rektörleri, akademisyenler ve kültür temsilcilerini bir araya getiren toplantının gündeminde, sanat üniversiteleri arasındaki işbirlikleri, ortak kültürel projeler ve uluslararası etkinliklere yönelik çalışmalar yer aldı.

Almanya 'da aşırı sağcı Almanya için Alternatif (AfD) partisi, cumhurbaşkanlığı seçimi için eski futbolcu Thomas Berthold'u aday gösterdi. Parti eş başkanları Alice Weidel ve Tino Chrupalla, 62 yaşındaki Berthold'un parti üyesi olmadığını özellikle vurguladı. Berthold'un özgeçmişinde 1990 Dünya Kupası şampiyonluğu da var, Adanaspor'da geçirdiği altı ay da.
Almanya için Alternatif'in eş başkanları Alice Weidel ve Tino Chrupalla, Berthold'u cumhurbaşkanlığı seçimine aday gösterdiklerini duyurdu. İki isim, 62 yaşındaki eski futbolcunun parti üyesi olmadığının altını çizdi. Weidel ve Chrupalla adayları için şu ifadeleri kullandı: 'Tüm Almanların cumhurbaşkanı olmaya son derece uygun.'
Berthold profesyonel kariyerine 1980'lerin başında Eintracht Frankfurt'ta başladı, ardından Bayern Münih ve VfB Stuttgart gibi Alman takımlarında forma giydi. Alman Milli Takımı formasıyla 60'tan fazla maça çıktı. 1990'da İtalya 'da düzenlenen Dünya Kupası'nı kazanan kadronun içinde yer aldı.
Ocak 2001'de Adanaspor'a transfer olan Berthold, Türkiye'de altı ay oynadıktan sonra Temmuz 2001'de futbolu bıraktı. Son yıllarda adı özellikle Covid-19 salgını sırasında alınan koruyucu önlemlere karşı çıkışlarıyla gündeme geldi.
Cumhurbaşkanı Frank-Walter Steinmeier'in görev süresi gelecek yılın başında sona erecek. Yerine CSU'lu siyasetçi Ilse Aigner'in 30 Ocak'ta seçilmesine kesin gözle bakılıyor. Aigner seçilirse Almanya 'nın ilk kadın devlet başkanı olacak. Adaylığı iktidardaki CDU/CSU ve SPD koalisyonunun yanı sıra muhalefetteki Yeşiller tarafından da destekleniyor.
