Türk müziğinin usta sanatçısı Nükhet Duru, katıldığı televizyon programında oğlu Cem Masis ile olan ilişkisini anlatırken duygusal anlar yaşadı. Bir annenin çocuğunu büyütürken geçirdiği değişimi anlatan sanatçı, oğlunun artık kendisini koruduğunu fark ettiği anları paylaşırken gözyaşlarına hakim olamadı.
Bloomberg HT ekranlarında Gözde Atasoy'un sunduğu "İşin Zirvesinde" programına konuk olan Nükhet Duru, annelik deneyiminden ve oğlu Cem Masis ile ilişkisinden söz etti.
Oğlunun büyüme sürecini anlatan sanatçı, bir zamanlar onu her şeyden korumaya çalışırken yıllar içinde rollerin değiştiğini ve artık oğlunun kendisini koruduğunu gördüğünü söyledi.
Bu anları anlatırken konuşmakta zorlanan Duru, gözyaşları içinde şu ifadeleri kullandı:
"Anne olarak onu dünyaya geldiğinde kucağına alıyorsun, büyümesini, küçücük ayakkabıların birden kapının arkasında kocaman bir ayakkabı haline gelmiş olmasını görüyorsun. Ve onu 'her şeyden koruyacağım' derken bir gün onun seni koruduğunu görüyorsun. Öyle güzel ki..."
Duygusal anların ardından çocuklara yönelik mesaj da veren sanatçı, ebeveyn olsun ya da olmasın herkesin çocuklara sevgi ve şefkatle yaklaşması gerektiğini vurguladı.
Normalde kolay kolay ağlayan biri olmadığını belirten Duru, sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü:
"Bütün evlat sahibi olanlara bunu diliyorum, olmayanlara da bütün çocuklar bizim aslında. Her çocuğa şefkat göstermeliyiz."
Nükhet Duru, 1987-1991 yılları arasında iş insanı Dikran Masis ile evli kaldı. Bu evlilikten Cem Masis dünyaya geldi.
Oğluyla arasındaki bağı anlatırken yaşadığı duygusal anlar, programın dikkat çeken bölümlerinden biri oldu.

Habertürk 'ten Onur Aydın'ın haberine göre; Nişantaşı'nda objektiflere yansıyan Canan Mutluer, Türk sinemasından güzellik algısı ve Türk dizilerinin başarısı üzerine konuştu. Güzellik algısının oyunculuğun önüne geçtiğini söyleyen Mutluer, "Aşırı dolgulu yüz ile seyirciye duyguyu geçiremezsiniz" dedi.
Canan Mutluer, daha sonra "Gözlerinizin gülmesi, gözlerinizin ağlaması gerekiyor. İlla salya sümük ağlamanız gerekmiyor ama gözlerinizle ifadeyi vermeniz gerekiyor. Gergin bir yüz ile bu ifadeyi veremezsiniz. Seyirciye geçmez ve seyirci terk eder. Ben o tarz isimleri izlemiyorum. Çok iyi bir izleyiciyim. Ben ekrana kitlenmişsem o iş tutuyor" ifadelerini kullandı. Canan Mutluer, Türk oyuncular arasında Halit Ergenç'i çok beğendiğini ifade ederek "Çok iyi kadın ve erkek oyuncularımız var. Halit Ergenç, muhteşem" diye konuştu.

Collins picked up a knee injury in the closing stages against Austria on Saturday
Republic of Ireland captain Nathan Collins has been ruled out of Tuesday's must-win Nations League game against Kosovo with a knee injury.
Defender Collins picked up the issue in the closing stages of Saturday's 1-0 defeat by Austria in Linz and has returned to his club Brentford for treatment.
Queens Park Rangers' Jimmy Dunne will replace Collins - who also missed all four games of the September/October window - in the matchday squad for the Kosovo fixture.
Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has opted against drafting in Seamus Coleman, who is currently with the squad in a playing/coaching hybrid role.
"No, Jimmy Dunne will take Nathan's spot but we're really happy with what Seamus is giving to us," said Hallgrimsson.
"We obviously need to see the session today, that's the first session after the game, to see how players are but given everything I think we'll have the same squad including Jimmy."
The Republic of Ireland must win Tuesday's game to finish second in Group B3 and seal a place in March's promotion play-offs.
Hallgrimsson's side fell to a late 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in September before bouncing back to take four points from two matches against Israel.
"We need to get the same mentality, the same characters on the pitch against Kosovo," added Hallgrimsson.
"It is going to be as tough a game as it was in Austria, so just transfer that same attitude and if we do that, we will have a good byproduct, which is a win.
"It is clear we need to win the game, a draw will do nothing for us, and that is our mentality going into the game."
The Republic of Ireland's ultimate aim is securing a place at Euro 2028, which they will co-host alongside England, Wales and Scotland.
While goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher said playing in a tournament at home would be "amazing", he insisted the players are not looking that far ahead.
"Yeah, it would obviously be hard to describe, it would be an amazing experience, to play in a major tournament at home would be special," said the Brentford keeper.
"But I don't think we can think too far ahead into that. Obviously we've got to focus on tomorrow and trying to get a good result and we'll look towards that then when it comes.
"But we all know the opportunity that's there for us if we can perform, so it'll be a great opportunity."

The Guardian’s new twice-weekly show unpicks all the biggest cultural moments. Plus, what is it like to grow up as a YouTube kidfluencer?
Is SNL UK funnier than the original? Does it matter if a pop star can sing? The Guardian’s Lanre Bakare and Carys Afoko host this twice-weekly culture videocast . On Thursdays, they zoom in on a big cultural moment with fresh takes. On Sundays, they have a culture swap: introducing each other to a TV series, book, film, album, play or podcast with which they’re obsessed. Hollie Richardson Widely available, episodes twice-weekly from Thursday 19 November
Every day someone in London calls an ambulance due to a chemsex-related emergency – but what’s being done to address the underlying causes of the harm queer people face in this world? In a thoughtful series, journalist Rory Boyle – a victim of a chemsex-related assault – discusses the issues with police officers, doctors, hook-up app employees and bereaved families. Rachel Aroesti Widely available, episodes weekly
This filmed podcast sees the ex-Channel 4 News presenter interview someone at the heart of a major news story. Despite the topics supposedly hailing from recent history, the first one tackles the 1984-5 miners’ strike via a sobering chat with Sherwood creator James Graham, who grew up in its aftermath – and funnelled its effects into TV drama. AD Widely available, episodes weekly

Hopes of promotion remain alive, but another costly collapse has raised familiar questions before the decisive Nations League game with Kosovo
T he Republic of Ireland stand on the verge, although of what, nobody seems quite sure. Tuesday’s final Nations League group match, at home to Kosovo, presents a chance for progress or yet another opportunity to showcase a frustrating habit of messing things up.
For 78 minutes in Linz on Saturday, Heimir Hallgrímsson’s side gave as good as they got against an Austria side who had not lost at home for a little more than three years. Set up in a compact, attack-minded formation they carried credible threat against hosts managed by Ralf Rangnick, but to nobody’s great surprise Sasa Kalajdzic broke the deadlock, scrambling home the winner from a needlessly conceded and poorly defended corner.
This late lapse neatly captures the contradiction bedevilling this Ireland team under Hallgrímsson. Over the past 12 months, Ireland have been unmistakably better than they were during the dark days of the post-pandemic slump under Stephen Kenny. They have established a clear identity and pulled off a couple of phenomenal wins with a spine of players performing at an elite level, supplemented by emerging talent from the leagues below and beyond. Yet for all that, an acceptable level of success remains elusive for a team who have not managed to shake a maddening habit of self-sabotage.
They have a high ceiling, as they demonstrated a year ago. Last November they dismantled Portugal at the Aviva Stadium in a World Cup qualifier before booking their place in the playoffs with an unforgettable come-from-behind win against Hungary at the Puskas Arena.
In Budapest, the celebrations of a dramatic Troy Parrott hat-trick completed in the sixth minute of added time went viral and elevated the then AZ striker from being surplus to the requirements of a dreadful Tottenham to sought-after European household name. For the first time in almost a decade, Ireland were playing with something resembling swagger, spearheaded by a poster-boy striker apparently entering his prime.
Riding that wave, Ireland travelled to Prague last March for the playoff semi-final against Czechia, with Parrott striking again, from the penalty spot, as they set about taking an early 2-0 lead. What followed would become the lowest point of Hallgrímsson’s reign as Ireland sat back and invited pressure before conceding a needless penalty and subsequent late equaliser that preceded a crushing shootout defeat . Despite last summer’s expanded 48-team format in North America, poor game management had stymied Ireland’s chances of making the cut.
An uninspiring, but unbeaten, summer friendly window featured fairly routine low-profile wins over Grenada and Qatar and a 1-1 draw against the World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal. Having steadied the ship before this Nations League campaign, Ireland produced a performance in their opener against Kosovo little short of diabolical and went down to another late goal.
In the subsequent four fixtures, two overshadowed by loud protests over Ireland’s decision to honour matches against Israel , that same cycle of promise and frustration has played out on a loop.
The disappointment of defeat in Pristina was immediately cancelled out by a clinical dispatch of Israel in Debrecen. In Dublin, against Austria , Parrott struck twice to give Ireland a commanding first-half lead, but in a collapse that rather mirrored their nightmarish Prague experience, Ireland went on to relinquish control and were forced to settle for a disappointing draw.
Three days later they coughed up another lead in a bad-tempered 1-1 draw with Israel, their compulsion for throwing away cheap points from winning positions coming back to bite them. Although they never led against Austria on Saturday, when Caoimhín Kelleher made a series of excellent saves, the winner they conceded was ridiculously soft.
Hallgrímsson’s appointment in July 2024 after a drawn-out process lasting eight months came as a surprise. He has built a side with a strong, if occasionally gaffe-prone, backbone including Kelleher, the goalkeeper’s Brentford teammate Nathan Collins and the Ipswich defender Dara O’Shea. Jack Moylan, having the season of his life at Cardiff, has impressed in midfield, and Southampton’s Finn Azaz is an occasional, but unreliable, source of creative guile. Parrott, enjoying life in La Liga with Real Betis, has evolved from promising talent to undisputed focal point of the attack.
To his credit, Hallgrímsson has forged a clear, pragmatic identity that maximises his team’s strengths without any delusions of fancy-dan footballing grandeur against elite opposition. Under his watch, Ireland are rarely outclassed and carry a cutting edge sorely absent in the dying days of his predecessor’s tenure.
Unfortunately, an inability to concentrate for 90 minutes continues to be their undoing and the must-win Nations League group finale at the Aviva Stadium will provide the ultimate judgment on the past 12 months. With Austria guaranteed promotion to League A, Ireland still have second place and its promotion playoff spot within reach.
Victory over Kosovo would also secure a place in pot two for next month’s Euro qualifying draw in Belfast, whereas defeat could leave them flirting with a relegation playoff to the tournament’s third tier. As the only ever-present residents of the Nations League’s second tier, now may be the time for something finally to give.

James Trafford has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026
As he was mobbed by his England team-mates for a late double save that secured England's memorable 3-2 win against world champions Spain on Sunday, the debate that followed about who the country's number one is was inevitable.
The Leeds stopper was given his chance to show England boss Thomas Tuchel what he could do again - and he absolutely took it.
On his fifth England cap the 24-year-old enjoyed a magnificent performance in Madrid as his side handed the hosts their first loss in 43 matches.
Trafford made four key saves in the final 12 minutes of the game, including an incredible double stop to first deny a Lamine Yamal curler and then dive again to his right to keep out Fermin Lopez from close range.
Last week England manager Thomas Tuchel had made it clear that Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford was his number one.
But after full-time in Spain Tuchel told ITV Sport "there's no number one" and Trafford had "a brilliant match".
So, following his performance on Sunday night, is Trafford now likely to oust Pickford as England's go-to goalkeeper?
Despite being just 24 years old Trafford has already been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee... twice.
Trafford returned to his boyhood Manchester City from Burnley for a £31m fee in 2025 and then left the Etihad for Leeds for £45m this summer - having been limited to being Pep Guardiola's 'cup goalkeeper'.
Given the downturn in form of their current goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, many City fans may well be wishing Trafford had stayed. Their loss is Leeds' - and maybe England's - gain.
At Leeds he has found his form and this season ranks first among the 52 goalkeepers who have played at least 10 games in Europe's big five leagues by save percentage (81.4%).
He has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026, and has rotated with Pickford across the Three Lions' five matches since the World Cup.
Pickford has started against Czech Republic and Croatia twice whereas Trafford has played against Czech Republic and started both England's matches with Spain, home and away.
After England's win in Madrid, which was the first time Spain had lost in the city in 39 years, Trafford's double-save was praised by his Three Lions team-mate Declan Rice.
"Everything happened so quick so for him to make two in the space of two seconds is massive," he told ITV. "A massive night for him."
Spain manager Luis de la Fuente agreed. He said: "We did generate some chances but England's goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes."
After the double-save several England players ran over to celebrate with Trafford.
And on Tuchel's decision to rotate between his two keepers former Manchester United captain Roy Keane told ITV: "I think it's smart management.
"This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing."
Social media has been full of the 'England number one' debate since, with many suggesting this was a moment that marked the changing of the guard.
Could Tuchel really now not start with Trafford for England's Nations League quarter-finals? Only time will tell.
What about Jordan Pickford though? England's undisputed first choice for almost 10 years has rarely let his country down.
Pickford, 32, has won 94 caps for England since making his debut in a 0-0 draw with Germany in 2017 and during his time as number one England have reached two World Cup semi-finals and two Euros finals.
According to Opta stats, Pickford has only made two errors leading to goals across his England career, with 46 clean sheets and a 74.3% save ratio.
And since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton.
"We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that," said former England number one goalkeeper Paul Robinson to BBC Sport before England's win against Spain,
"It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period.
"This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency plan, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has said as much.
"I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection."
This isn't a debate that is going away any time soon. But having two goalkeepers genuinely competing for that number one shirt can only be to England's benefit.
60 minutes of perfection, 30 minutes of chaos - an England win for the ages
How did England cling on against Spain and what did Tuchel do differently?

There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak
L ast week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result.
Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so.
But for all the familiarity and continuity for the Socceroos – five players who were there when Son Heung-min broke Australian hearts featured in Friday’s win – being back in Doha rams home just how much has changed for this team, and how well and truly into a new era we are.
Tony Popovic occupies the dugout these days, after the defeat to Korea arguably represented the beginning of the end of Arnold’s tenure by sparking a fatigue that would culminate in a downturn in results and his resignation later that year.
Nestory Irankunda, the rapidly emerging star of Popovic’s team who now has eight international goals to his name, was about to suffer a 4-0 defeat against the Central Coast Mariners nearly three years ago. Alessandro Circati was left out of the Socceroos squad to ensure he retained his place in the Parma side seeking to secure promotion to Serie A. Paul Okon-Engstler, Patrick Beach and Lucas Herrington were all yet to play senior football.
These players, who all started against Qatar, are emerging cornerstones of a new Socceroos setup that fielded the World Cup’s youngest side in North America, before flashing signs of further growth against Brazil in September. On Friday, this talented group bullied the two-time defending Asian champions on their own turf in the first-half, putting the game to bed before Popovic swung the changes and things got disjointed after half-time.
There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality. Of players bringing to the national team the lessons they’ve learned not just in the green and gold, but also in their experiences at bigger, more demanding clubs and leagues – in part because of the platform they’ve been offered by Popovic.
All of which could make it serendipitous if Tuesday’s game against Jordan, at the symbolic home of his predecessor, proves to be the end of the Popovic era.
The players aren’t going anywhere but with his contract situation still up in the air, it could well prove to be Popovic’s last game in charge of the Socceroos if he doesn’t agree to an extension. Given the postponement of January’s Asian Cup , there may not be the send-off he might have envisioned. Instead, a 12,000-seat stadium – unlikely to be very full – will host a hastily-relocated friendly that’s entire raison d’être has vanished.
Remarkably, after sensitive discussions to relocate Tuesday’s game after player resistance to travelling to Amman, in line with DFAT advice , Doha could once again be pressed into action to serve as a historic backdrop for the Socceroos, just as a pandemic already saw it become the site of many a moment of distinction.

Brazilian legend, an investor at Serie C club, showed glimpses of old brilliance as he played 45 minutes for the promotion-chasing side
I t may have been the longest buildup in world football. In June, the former Barcelona and Brazil legend Ronaldinho was unveiled by the Serie C side Ravenna to make his comeback at the age of 46 – 11 years after his last official game. Then silence.
But on a chilly November day on the eastern coast of Italy, there he was , not only in the squad, but in the starting XI for the eagerly anticipated derby against Forlì as Ravenna chase promotion.
The Ravenna manager, Andrea Mandorlini, deployed Ronaldinho in a central position, just behind the striker Simone Rabbi. The Brazilian held his position well, but was slow to get going. As the game progressed, he warmed up and showed his excellent skills; some things do not appear to change. Ronaldinho touched the ball 25 times, took three corners – one of which nearly led to a Ravenna goal – and initiated the move that led to the hosts taking the lead in the 35th minute.
Having trained with the team just once, whether he plays again remains to be seen. But he had already sprinkled some magic on a club and a region that has not made headlines in years. He played the first half as Ravenna won 2-0 to stay second in the division’s Group B (the Italian third tier is divided into three regional sections). Only the group winners earn promotion and Ravenna trail Spezia by six points.
Whatever happens for the remainder of the season this has put the club back on the football map. Ravenna’s highest finish was eighth in Serie B, in 1996-97, but this match was broadcast live by Sky Sports in Italy and shown in several other countries. It even appeared on the giant screens in New York’s Times Square, where the club’s owners, the Cipriani family, have built much of their international reputation through Harry’s Bar.
The town’s mayor, Alessandro Barattoni, who, as always, was watching the game from the stands, said: “A champion like Ronaldinho, a world football icon, brings great visibility and today is an opportunity for us to showcase Ravenna around the world, from our stadium. It is something new for us and together with the club the municipality will try to understand how this can have a positive impact on the town.”
The local community had been excited at the prospect of Ronaldinho representing the club, but there was some regret, too. “It would have been nice if he had come to take a stroll around the city, among the people who live here and own the shops,” the barista Barbara said before the game.
So how did he end up here? The Brazilian is a friend of Ignazio Cipriani, the owner of the Giallorossi . Lorenzo Tonetti and Ariedo Braida, old acquaintances from Ronaldinho’s time at Milan, are also part of the club. They convinced him to become an investor in the club and to pull on his boots again. In addition, Ravenna are now wearing his R10 sportswear line and one of the stands bears the same name.
Ravenna are aiming high. Cipriani has never hidden the fact he is aiming for Serie A, which is ambitious for a city with a population of 156,000. And Sunday brought hope, Dinho stepping on to the pitch in a gold-trimmed kit picked by the club to celebrate his arrival (and available for sale at €120). His hair was kept in check by a black headband and he was wearing gloves on a chilly afternoon. On his back, the No 10, something more than just a number for him, the man who became a global hero thanks to his extraordinary skill and contagious smile.
A younger generation has been able to discover Ronaldinho’s genius through the endless supply of online videos showcasing his greatest moments. Children who have never seen him play know his tricks and signature moves, while their parents can relive an era of football they may feel no longer exists.
“Dad, was he strong?” a young girl asked her father as they walked hand in hand towards the stadium. “Yes, he was strong. Actually, he is strong,” he corrected himself.
One family had left Rome at 5am and travelled the 350km north just because their son had watched Ronaldinho on YouTube and wanted to see him live. Others had travelled even further, with supporters arriving from Turkey and Canada.
Ronaldinho hahas scored 299 professional goals, but his landmark 300th on his return was not to be. However, in front of a record attendance of 6,743 the way he initiated the move for Giulio Donati’s goal was ample reward for those who had turned up. Donati made his Serie A debut on 29 August 2010 for Lecce, at San Siro, against Milan, marking the Brazilian that day.
As Ronaldinho walked off at half-time, he was surrounded by a media scrum. After the game, he spoke of his desire to play again. “It all went by too quickly,” he said. “Football is like that, it’s always been like that for me.”
Who knows, perhaps he enjoyed himself so much that he wants to extend his career even further. “I don’t know, but if the president calls me, I’ll come back. It’s always a pleasure to play, I told him: ‘when he needs me, I’m there’.”
Mandorlini was effusive too. “We’re here and we’re truly proud to have been the architects of this match you played in,” he told the Brazilian. “So, if you want to play another one, that’s fine.”
Who knows what the future holds? For now, Ravenna fans will always have this: a day when a true legend connected people from around the world and allowed them, for one afternoon, to dream.

Mary McAteer celebrates after scoring Ipswich's opening goal at Watford
Ipswich Town boss David Wright praised the football intelligence of Wales international Mary McAteer following her first goal for the club.
McAteer joined Town on loan from Charlton Athletic in September as part of a revamp of the squad following last season's ninth-place finish in Women's Super League 2.
She headed home the rebound after skipper Maria Boswell's fierce shot came back off the crossbar against Watford and they went on to win Sunday's game 2-1.
The victory put Town third - and in the play-off places - in only their second season at that level.
"Every time Bos gets the ball in that area now, in my head I'm thinking, 'just shoot'," Wright told BBC Radio Suffolk.
"Mary is a really intelligent footballer - she uses her intelligence to find space between the lines, it allows her link through the thirds, and it's another sign of her intelligence that when Bos hits a beautiful strike, it hits the bar, bounces down, she's the first one to react and nods it in."
Kit Graham added Ipswich's second as they bounced back positively from a 2-1 home league defeat by Bristol City and midweek loss to McAteer's parent club Charlton in the Players' Cup.
"It has been a really tough week, not just physically, but also psychologically - three different challenges," said Wright.
"What good teams do is they bounce back. To finish the week off, going to Watford and coming away with three points, the girls should be really proud of themselves."
Boswell said last month that she believes it is "inevitable" that Town will eventually achieve their goal of a place in the top flight of English women's football.
But despite their current position, Wright insisted it was not a focus for him.
"I don't really look at the table. I want to push them, make them better and if we do that we will keep moving in the right direction - that process is getting better every day and will help us achieve what we want to achieve," he said.
Wright's side have won five of their eight WSL 2 games but now have over a month to wait before the next, when they travel to bottom-of-the-table Durham.
"I was looking at the calendar on the wall and I've never known such a big gap. The good thing is we've got lots of games in between so we'll be busy and when the Durham game comes round, the girls will be ready," Wright added.

The Union of European Clubs has submitted a formal complaint against the stranglehold Uefa and European Football Clubs maintain on football within the continent, dramatically escalating its efforts to obtain recognition by governing bodies and dilute the power held by the elite.
The complaint, filed to the European Commission on Monday, challenges the memorandum of understanding (MoU) between EFC and Uefa . That agreement, which runs until July 2033, stipulates that EFC is the “sole body” representing European clubs. The UEC, which was founded three years ago and has 138 members from 25 national associations, aims to afford a voice to those beyond the established powers and has long sought to be allowed a formal presence in the corridors of power. It believes a select group of leading clubs hold decisive influence over the fate of those beneath them, including their prospects of access to competitions such as the Champions League and Europa League.
A fundamental pillar of the complaint is the assertion that the MoU breaches Article 101 of the EU Treaty, which bans anti-competitive agreements, and Article 102, which bans abuse of a dominant position. According to the status quo, no club may join another cross-border club association unless EFC and Uefa grant permission. EFC is understood to have told at least one club that its membership would be terminated if it opted simultaneously to remain within UEC.
According to the complaint, 59 of UEC’s member clubs asked upon joining that their membership status not be made public, citing concerns about the potential for pressure to be applied. The UEC’s stance is that EFC, which is closing in on 1,000 members after an accelerated recruitment drive in recent years, should not hold an exclusive mandate. It points out that, despite EFC’s swollen numbers, the organisation’s clubs do not hold equal voting rights despite a series of recent reforms.
“The question is simple: who gets a say in the rules that shape every club’s future,” said Dennis Gudasic, the UEC general secretary and CEO of the Croatian top-flight club Lokomotiva Zagreb. “Today one association holds that mandate for all of Europe’s clubs, while most clubs have no effective voice in it. We are asking the commission to examine whether that is compatible with EU law, and to help open European football’s governance to the whole pyramid.”
Miguel Maduro, a former chair of Fifa’s governance and review committee, advised UEC on the complaint. “This case is about using European competition law to protect the European sports model of genuinely open and balanced competitions,” Maduro said. “A system where a select group of elite clubs is given the power to decide who gets to compete in European competitions, and how the revenues are distributed, does not only harm competition in European and national football. It gradually destroys the model of open and balanced competition that Uefa itself claims to protect.”
Over the past 18 months the UEC has proposed a number of measures that would, it believes, improve the flow of money to clubs beneath the game’s giants. Last year it put forward a “player development reward”; under that scheme, another 5% of revenue from club competitions would be redistributed to the teams whose academies developed those competing in them. It has also created a model for the reinvestment of club competition media rights into domestic leagues. Neither proposal has been given a serious hearing by more established powers.
It may take at least four months for the EC to decide whether to open the investigation demanded by UEC, which is understood to be open to withdrawing the complaint if the problems it highlights are resolved via a binding agreement. A competition law complaint by European Leagues against Fifa, filed to the EC more than two years ago, is yet to reach any resolution.

Oyuncu Alina Boz ile yönetmen eşi Umut Evirgen , İstanbul Etiler'de arkadaşlarıyla yemek yedikleri bir mekânın çıkışında görüntülendi. İlk bebeğini bekleyen Boz, soğuk havaya rağmen muhabirlerin sorularını kısaca yanıtladı; eşiyle birlikte spora başladıklarını söyledi ve ortaya çıkan sonucu gülerek anlattı.
Posta'nın aktardığına göre Boz, hamileliğinin çok güzel geçtiğini belirtti. Eşiyle aynı dönemde spora başladıklarını anlatan oyuncu, "İkimiz de spora başladık, ama bir terslik var. Ben kilo aldım, o zayıfladı" sözleriyle Evirgen'e takıldı.
Arkadaşlarıyla yemek yediklerini belirten çift, mekân çıkışındaki sohbeti uzatmadı. Boz ve Evirgen, "Hava çok soğuk, sonra konuşuruz" diyerek mekânın önünden ayrıldı.
Alina Boz, geniş kitlelerce "Paramparça" dizisinde canlandırdığı Hazal karakteriyle tanındı. Oyuncu sonraki yıllarda "Vatanım Sensin" ve "Maraşlı" dizilerinde, "Bandırma Füze Kulübü" filminde rol aldı. Umut Evirgen ise yönetmen kimliğiyle biliniyor.
Aralık 2023'te hayatlarını birleştiren Boz ve Evirgen, evliliklerini gözlerden uzak yaşamayı tercih ediyor. Oyuncu, bebek beklediğini daha önce katıldığı bir mezuniyet töreninde kendisi doğrulamıştı.
Çift, ilk çocuklarını kucaklarına almaya hazırlanıyor. Boz ve Evirgen'in Etiler'deki görüntüleri ile oyuncunun spor sözleri, Hürriyet ve Sabah'ın magazin sayfalarında da yer aldı.

Dünya El Nino hava olayına karşı alarmda. Rekor sıcaklara ve rekor yağışlara neden olan El Nino için yeni uyarı Meteoroloji Mühendisi Mikdat Kadıoğlu'ndan geldi. Prof. Dr. Mikdat Kadıoğlu, 'Türkiye'de 2027 kışı nasıl geçecek? Çok kar yağacak mı?' sorularını yanıtladı.
Meteoroloji Mühendisi Prof. Dr. Mikdat Kadıoğlu, El Nino hava olaylarına dair yeni açıklamalarda bulundu. TGRT Haber'den Zeynep Gizem Er'e konuşan Kadıoğlu, '2027 kışı nasıl geçecek?' sorusunu da yanıtladı.
'Kasım ve aralık aylarının ortalamadan sıcak geçeceğine ilişkin bir tahmin, bütün kışın sıcak geçeceğini veya kar yağmayacağını göstermez. Mevsimlik tahminler, belirli bir dönemin genel eğilimini anlatır; tek tek günlerde yaşanacak hava olaylarını değil. WMO da bu ayrımı açıkça vurguluyor: Bunlar mevsimlik görünümlerdir, tekil olayların tahmini değildir.
Bunu şöyle düşünebiliriz: Bir ayın çoğu günü ılık geçerken birkaç gün çok soğuk olabilir. Dolayısıyla 'ortalamanın üzerinde sıcaklık' ile 'hiç soğuk olmayacak' aynı şey değildir. WMO’nun ekim –aralık görünümünde de ortalamadan sıcak bir dönem beklentisinin her yerin her gün ortalamadan sıcak olacağı anlamına gelmediği belirtiliyor.'
Prof. Dr. Mikdat Kadıoğlu'na göre 'Çok kar yağacak, şu illere kar yağacak gibi' cümleler için pek çok etken göz önünde bulundurulmalı. Kadıoğlu, sözlerine şöyle devam etti:
'El Niño’nun güçlü olması da tek başına Türkiye için bir kar haritası oluşturmaz. Etkiler mevsime, coğrafi konuma ve Hint ile Atlas okyanuslarındaki koşullar gibi diğer etkenlere göre değişebilir. Bu yüzden yalnızca El Niño’ya bakarak İstanbul ’a kar yağmayacak, şu illerde ağır kış olacak ya da bu bölgede kesin kuraklık yaşanacak demek, mevcut bilginin taşıyabileceğinden daha kesin konuşmaktır.
Hangi il ve bölgelerin daha fazla risk altında olduğunu söylemek için önce hangi riskten söz edildiği açıklanmalıdır: Yoğun kar mı, don mu, yağış azlığı mı, taşkın mı? Bunların her biri ayrı değerlendirme gerektirir. İl adı vererek yapılacak uyarıların dayanağı, ulusal ve yerel tahminler olmalıdır; küresel bir iklim olayının adı değil. Resmî uyarıların yetkili kaynağı ulusal meteoroloji servisleridir.'

Amerikan Basketbol Ligi'nde (NBA) Houston Rockets, milli oyuncu Alperen Şengün'ün "triple-double"a yaklaştığı maçta Washington Wizards'ı 147-119 yendi.
Capital One Arena'da Wizards'a konuk olan Rockets'ta yaklaşık 28 dakika süre alan Alperen Şengün, 19 sayı, 8 ribaunt, 8 asist, 2 top çalmayla takımının galibiyetine katkı sağladı.
Üst üste 4 olmak üzere 11. galibiyetini alan Rockets'ta Amen Thompson 26, Kevin Durant ve Tari Eason 25'er sayı attı.
Wizards'ta ise Alex Sarr'ın 25 ve AJ Dybantsa'nın 16 sayısı, peş peşe 7, sezonun 10. mağlubiyetini engelleyemedi.
Philadelphia 76ers forması giyen LeBron James, NBA tarihinin asist sıralamasında Jason Kidd'i geride bıraktı.
LeBron James, takımının Indiana Pacers'ı 131-124 yendiği mücadelede 15 sayı, 11 asistle mücadele etti. Kariyerinde 12 bin 92 asiste ulaşan James, NBA'de tüm zamanların asist sıralamasında Kidd'i (12 bin 91) geçerek üçüncü basamağa yerleşti. John Stockton (15 bin 806) ve Chris Paul (12 bin 552), James'in önünde ilk iki sırada yer aldı.
Sezonun 11. galibiyetine ulaşan 76ers'ta Jaylen Brown 31 ve Tyrese Maxey 27 sayıyla oynadı.
Pacers'ta Pascal Siakam'ın 31 ve Kelly Oubre Jr'ın 16 sayısı, sezonun 9. mağlubiyetini önleyemedi.
Los Angeles Lakers, Mortgage Matchup Center'da konuk olduğu Phoenix Suns'ı 131-123 mağlup etti.
Art arda 8, bu sezon 12. galibiyetini elde eden Lakers'ta Luka Doncic, 43 sayı, 9 asist ve Quentin Grimes 22 sayı, 6 ribaunt üretti.
Sezonun 7. yenilgisini yaşayan Suns'ta ise Collin Gillespie 26 ve Luke Kennard 18 sayı kaydetti.

Coca-Cola Arena'da oynanacak karşılaşma saat 19.00'da başlayacak.
Ligde oynadığı 11 maçta 5 galibiyet, 6 yenilgi yaşayan Anadolu Efes, 12. sırada yer alıyor. Lacivert-beyazlı ekip, ligde oynadığı son maçında İtalya'nın Virtus Bologna takımını 103-91 yendi.
11. haftada Olympiakos'a 101-72 yenilen Dubai Basketbol 7 galibiyet, 4 mağlubiyetle 9. sırada bulunuyor.
Anadolu Efes, Dubai Basketbol maçıyla Avrupa'da 925. kez sahne alacak.
Lacivert-beyazlılar, Avrupa kupalarında geride kalan 924 karşılaşmada 511 galibiyet, 413 yenilgi yaşadı.
Anadolu Efes, 2001-2002 sezonundan itibaren yer aldığı Avrupa Ligi'nde ise 677. maçını yapacak. Ligdeki 676 müsabakanın 354'ünü kazanan lacivert-beyazlılar, 322'sinde mağlup oldu.
İlk kez geçen sezon birbirlerine rakip olan iki takımın geride kalan 2 maçta birer galibiyeti bulunuyor.
